* * *
# Iran
* **Russia, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and China push for renewed U.S.-Iran diplomacy; Tehran demands return to MOU:** Russia and Saudi Arabia are seeking "compromise solutions" to implement the memorandum of understanding between the U.S. and Iran, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said on Tuesday after talks with his Saudi counterpart, Prince Faisal bin Farhan.
* Lavrov said the two countries "regret" that Arab states have been "dragged against their will" into the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran.
* Separately, Qatar said it is working with China and other countries to revive U.S.-Iran talks.
* Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi said the Gulf conflict is threatening regional security and disrupting energy markets, shipping and supply chains. "Pressure through guns and cannons is not the way out. Dialogue and negotiation are the right path," Wang said.
* Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, meanwhile, blamed Washington's "regrettable" violation of the MOU. "The solution is simple; the return and adherence of the American side to its commitments and signing of the memorandum of understanding will pave the way for a return to normalcy," Araghchi [said](https://substack.com/redirect/dc81eaec-547d-44c1-adf3-8d15f682748f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* **Iran hikes gas prices for heaviest consumers:** Iran introduced a price hike for its heaviest gasoline users, according to state media, as the economy continues to suffer as a result of the U.S. blockade, the second such increase since December. Under the new regulations, people buying more than their quota of 110 liters (29 gallons) of gas a month--roughly 15% of consumers--must now pay twice as much.
* **Amnesty: U.S.-Israeli attacks on Tehran in March may amount to war crimes:** U.S.-Israeli attacks on three neighborhoods in Tehran in March that killed and wounded dozens of civilians may amount to war crimes, according to a new [report](https://substack.com/redirect/a9553043-5ec2-4f30-a86b-3d8a2261c879?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by Amnesty International. The investigation into air strikes on Niloofar, Resalat, and Javadieh neighborhoods in Tehran between March 1 and 13, 2026 found evidence that "explosive weapons with wide area effects were used in densely populated areas, killing and injuring civilians" and causing widespread and extensive damage to homes.
* "The civilian death toll, the scale of destruction, the timing of the attacks, the impact on nearby civilian structures and the lack of effective advance warnings point to alarming failures by the U.S.-Israeli coalition...to minimize civilian harm and spare civilian objects," Agnes Callamard, Secretary General of Amnesty International, said in a statement. "The U.S./Israeli strikes in Teheran investigated by Amnesty International, may constitute indiscriminate attacks and amount to war crimes."
* Drop Site covered two of the three March attacks investigated in the Amnesty investigation. Read our reports on the U.S.-Israeli bombings of**[ Nilofoor](https://substack.com/redirect/4c0ca3d0-a7b7-493b-8b2b-1302de44ceaf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **and **[Resalat](https://substack.com/redirect/e070b92a-79c5-44bb-9b00-e8eb54919e00?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**.
* **Iranian Basij commander killed in "terrorist attack": **Abdolrauf Eshaghi, a commander in Iran's paramilitary Basij forces, was killed in an attack on Tuesday, according to Iranian state media. Authorities described the incident as a "terrorist attack," but it was not immediately clear who was responsible.

# Palestine
* **Elderly Palestinian man injured by Israeli fire in Gaza; Israel issues forced displacement orders:** Israeli forces [shot and injured](https://substack.com/redirect/a56dca83-60eb-452d-8ccb-7ae1cdcb0d98?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an elderly Palestinian man south of Khan Younis on Tuesday, Al Jazeera reported.
* Since Tuesday morning, Israeli forces have issued at least five forced displacement orders across Gaza. Orders were reported in Al-Bureij, Nuseirat, Gaza City near Al-Shifa Hospital, and at two locations in Al-Shati refugee camp. One of the warned sites, a home near Al-Shifa Hospital, was subsequently hit with three missiles.
* **Israeli forces kill four Palestinians, carry out raids and closures across occupied West Bank:** In the past 24 hours, Israeli forces [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/6545b341-4c3e-4305-92ed-04cf161cd68c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) four Palestinians in Qalqilya, Nablus, and Tulkarem governorates, bringing the number of Palestinians killed in the occupied West Bank since the start of the year to 100, according to the Palestinian Health Ministry.
* **Bethlehem:** Israeli forces detained two Palestinian teens during a raid in central Bethlehem, according to WAFA. Soldiers also assaulted and injured one of the boys' mothers.
* **Nablus:** An Israeli settler was reportedly stabbed multiple times near Aqraba. Israeli forces subsequently closed all entrances to Aqraba and neighboring villages and launched a search for the suspect.
* **UK announces ban on Israeli settlement goods; France and Canada to follow:** The UK [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/162dab2f-ce23-4fee-8c53-86349fad14aa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a ban on trade in goods produced in illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank and sanctions targeting individuals and companies involved in settlement expansion on Tuesday, with Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband calling the move "the beginning of a new approach, to call out injustice and to act." He added, "The British government agrees that there is ethnic cleansing of Palestinians in areas of the West Bank, perpetrated by settler terrorists."
* In a [statement](https://substack.com/redirect/785ae5d7-0bd0-4c34-ad86-3e6809d63087?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the British Palestinian Committee said, "Today's announcement, while welcome, will ultimately be judged not by its rhetoric, but by its enforcement both within and beyond this current government."
* According to [Bloomberg](https://substack.com/redirect/34e6d4e0-d869-4730-801b-94396b2a48e5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), British diplomats "privately told the US that the sanctions are largely symbolic and will have no material impact on the UK's wider relationship with Israel on trade or security, in a bid to soothe the Trump administration's response." Reuters [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/5d0c69f3-a9e0-4390-bbb9-78a11477ca4a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that the impact of the policy move on bilateral trade with Israel is "likely to be minimal, with details unclear of how the UK will differentiate between goods originating in West Bank settlements [and] products made in Israel."
* France said it would begin its own process to ban settlement products, while Canada is also expected to join the action.
* "Why are we doing this? Because the West Bank is close to exploding," French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot [wrote](https://substack.com/redirect/f0c0d1e0-27b7-45bd-9908-334cceeab696?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on X, continuing, "there is frenzied expansion of the settlements, a flare-up of violence against Palestinians by extremist settlers, and acts of terror which have been attacked by Israeli authorities themselves."
* **Haaretz: UAE warned Netanyahu before Oct. 7, but Netanyahu didn 't tell security chiefs**: UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed personally [warned](https://substack.com/redirect/fa8f3631-8352-446f-97f5-2e96bd5cb1c7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in a 45-minute call roughly a week and a half before October 7, 2023, that Hamas leader Yahya Sinwar was planning a major operation, according to a Haaretz investigation.
* Netanyahu reportedly reacted calmly, insisted Hamas intended to strike the West Bank, and never briefed the heads of Shin Bet, Mossad, or the IDF about the warning.
* In the months preceding MBZ's warning, Hamas leadership reportedly indicated that it was planning an operation, using a secret backchannel for discussions (through a Fatah intermediary) to warn Israel of a coming "zilzal," or earthquake. That message reached the Shin Bet on September 15 and prompted a security meeting, though no action was taken.
* Former Shin Bet chief Ronen Bar and former IDF Chief of Staff Herzl Halevi both said they were never informed of MBZ's warning. Bin Zayed did not respond to Haaretz's request for comment.

# Yemen
* **Yemeni Saudi-backed forces launch attacks on Ansarallah positions, vow to retake Sana 'a: **Forces aligned with Yemen's Saudi-backed government launched attacks against Ansarallah positions, as Deputy Defense Minister Samir Al-Sabri said "the decision has been made to retake Sana'a."
* Fighting intensified in Al-Bayda and Al-Jawf governorates, which lie on routes towards the Ansarallah-held capital.
* Ansarallah said seven people were killed in a strike on a prison in Al-Hazm, Al-Jawf.

* **Ansarallah attacks injure 73; hit Saudi energy facilities:** The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen [said](https://substack.com/redirect/1daad903-2eb3-4d51-85be-f36204c0cc46?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) recent Ansarallah attacks on Saudi Arabia injured 73 people, including women and children. Coalition spokesperson Turki Al-Maliki said its forces would take measures to "deter" Ansarallah and counter further threats.
* Separately, Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry [said](https://substack.com/redirect/3023911b-a2a2-4334-90bc-3ce6fe442652?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) several energy facilities in the south were hit on Tuesday, causing injuries and fires and temporarily disrupting operations at some sites. Satellite imagery showed plumes of smoke rising from Aramco's Jizan refinery.
* **Report: Yemen clashes displace 18,500:** Renewed fighting across Yemen's Taiz and Hodeidah governorates [displaced](https://substack.com/redirect/4cd33d4c-3a6b-486a-9d85-816ced16c131?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) about 18,500 people since hostilities escalated on September 3 with the number "increasing by the hour," according to the International Organization for Migration (IOM), putting further pressure on already overstretched communities in southern Taiz and along the west coast. "Families are arriving with nothing: no shelter, no food, no way to know if it's safe to go back," IOM Yemen chief Abdusattor Esoev said, noting that many have been displaced multiple times.
* The agency said ongoing clashes and disrupted telecommunications are hampering aid access, while emergency food and shelter stocks have been severely depleted by recent flood responses.

# Lebanon
* **Israeli attacks kill 12 in southern Lebanon as attacks continue despite "ceasefire":**
* In Kfar Remman, an Israeli airstrike after midnight Monday destroyed a three-story residential building killing 11 members of the same family, including two children and four women, and wounded eight others.
* An Israeli drone also struck a vehicle in Kfar Remman, killing one paramedic from the Islamic Risala Scout Association and wounding two others.
* Israeli forces raided Kfarchouba at dawn and raised an Israeli flag on one of the surrounding hills in the Hasbaya district, according to Lebanon 24.
* Israeli attacks killed 4,381 people and wounded 12,402 between March 2 and September 7, according to Lebanon's Health Ministry.

# U.S. News
* **Socialist wave headed for Providence:** State Rep. **David Morales** is threatening to become the third socialist to sweep into power in an American city this year, after New York City and Seattle. Incumbent Mayor **Brett Smiley** trailed the **Bernie Sanders** -backed Morales in the most recent survey, sponsored by an ally of Morales. The local DSA has not endorsed fellow DSA member Morales; their bylaws ban them from endorsing a candidate running as a Democrat.
* A November ballot initiative has featured prominently in the race. The measure does not mention Israel but would bar the city from making investments in "foreign countries conducting ethnic cleansing, apartheid, illegal military occupation or genocide." [Israel supporters in the city ](https://substack.com/redirect/3d857f86-4daa-4c87-b4cb-8dcc2afd04f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)have launched a campaign in opposition to the referendum; Mayor Smiley opposes it, while Morales supports it.
* The race has otherwise played out along familiar lines, with Morales backing off his previous pledges to "defund the police" while promising to focus on making Providence more affordable for working people, while Smiley has maintained the support of the city's landlords, developers, and major business owners. [Watch Morales's interview on Breaking Points](https://substack.com/redirect/1089a652-eae0-4a1e-b292-918bcbdc859f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* **New Hampshire Senate, House primaries Tuesday:** In the Senate primary, insurgent challenger **Karishma Manzur** , [a refugee from Bangladesh whose father ](https://substack.com/redirect/c7b54b0f-ed1e-49fc-838f-4f9c6a26728b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)was assassinated after helping win the nation's independence, is challenging Rep. **Chris Pappas** , who is facing a closer-than-expected contest as Manzur has highlighted her opposition to genocide and aligned herself with the Mamdani wing of the party. A recent internal Pappas poll had him ahead by more than 50 points, but a University of New Hampshire survey found Manzur behind by just 13 points. In the race to replace Pappas, two center-left candidates, including the daughter of Sen. **Jeanne Shaheen** , are leading in polls.

* **Armed man attacks Ohio gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton:** An armed individual [attacked](https://substack.com/redirect/d6570ff8-1eb8-4086-b3f3-c70e5a964f27?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Ohio Democratic gubernatorial candidate **Amy Acton** on Sunday at the Canfield Fair near Youngstown, according to her campaign and the state highway patrol, though Acton was not harmed in the incident.
* The suspect, 38-year-old **Patrick Havas,** knocked over multiple people while trying to reach Acton and was carrying a taser and two pistols. Police charged him with disorderly conduct and two counts of assault.
* **Canada 's retaliatory tariffs on $20 billion of U.S. goods take effect: **New Canadian tariffs on roughly $20 billion in U.S. imports, including clothing, cheese, metal parts, and wood products, took effect Tuesday, mirroring earlier U.S. duties imposed after trade talks between the two countries collapsed last month.
* Hours before the tariffs took effect, President Donald Trump attacked Canadian plane maker Bombardier on social media, declaring "NO MORE SELLING BOMBARDIER IN THE UNITED STATES!"
* Bombardier noted in response that it employs "tens of thousands" of American workers and manufactures wings in California and Texas.
* A new round of U.S. tariffs on additional countries is expected as soon as this week. The Supreme Court previously struck down Trump's duties in February.
* **New York residents misled about air quality following 9/11, documents show:** New York City officials [found](https://substack.com/redirect/414a7a2a-94d0-40e5-ae26-6af36098403f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) evidence of asbestos and other contaminants in Lower Manhattan for months after the September 11 attacks, even as the city publicly assured residents the air was safe, according to 170,000 pages of previously hidden air quality reports and internal correspondence released by Tuesday.
* The documents were discovered last year and released by Mayor **Zohran Mamdani** to coincide with the attacks' 25th anniversary.
* Rep.**Jerrold Nadler,** whose district included the World Trade Center, said of the Giuliani and Bloomberg administrations, "they knew about the air quality, and they essentially did nothing about it... I suspect that all they cared about was getting Wall Street reopened."
* **Mamdani creates Mayor 's Office of Worker Power to boost labor organizing**: Mamdani signed an executive order on Monday creating an Office of Worker Power to support private-sector labor organizing in New York City.
* The office will be led by **Tony Perlstein** , a former UAW organizing director, who said its goal is to help workers "stand up and speak up" against wealthy employers who can "afford to pay their workers more."
* Deputy Mayor for Economic Justice **Julie Su** , to whom Perlstein will report, clarified that the office "will not be directly going into workplaces and organizing workers" but instead will hold hearings, share information on worker rights, and refer participants to unions and worker centers.
* **ICE granted permission to force-feed Cuban detainee via surgical stomach tube** : A federal judge in Texas [approved](https://substack.com/redirect/1ba15306-9ab6-4b5a-8d05-dc5de85e9a36?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) ICE's request to force-feed a Cuban hunger striker held at the privately run Montgomery ICE processing center, including through a rare, nonconsensual surgical procedure involving a permanent gastric feeding tube, according to court records reported on by The Guardian.
* Judge **Andrew Hanen** initially authorized the force-feeding on August 19 and extended the order this week, though DHS said Thursday the man had "resumed eating and drinking again" and was not currently being force-fed.
* The man, arrested by ICE on July 22 and declared a hunger striker three days later, lacks legal representation.
* Since January 2025, the agency has received court approval at least 19 times for involuntary medical procedures on hunger strikers.
* **U.S. forces raid vessel in Eastern Pacific and detain crew:** U.S. forces raided a vessel in the Eastern Pacific on Monday, detaining everyone on board, [according](https://substack.com/redirect/aa64d7b5-d3d0-4e77-a70a-b34d53fe228c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to U.S. Southern Command (SOUTHCOM), which posted a video of the attack and saying the vessel was "supporting illicit at-sea drug trafficking" without providing evidence. "After clearing the vessel and disembarking the crew, U.S. forces sank it," SOUTHCOM said.

# Other International News
* **Far-right AfD party wins state election in eastern Germany:** The Alternative for Germany party [won](https://substack.com/redirect/a6ae15fd-8797-4fc4-b2f1-c41a8e24a28b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) elections in Germany's Saxony-Anhalt state while securing 39 of 83 seats, leaving it three short of a governing majority. If the AfD succeeds in forming a government, it would become the first far-right party to control a German state since World War II, gaining authority over areas including policing, education, and culture.
* Several parties ruled out cooperation with the AfD, raising the possibility of a minority government, defections from other parties, or another election.
* The AfD's state branch is officially classified as a right-wing extremist organization by Germany's domestic intelligence and the party has been criticized within Germany for alleged support for Russia.
* **Nine killed in explosion at Bolivian military base:** Bolivian authorities said that nine people were [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/761c5adf-e0a7-4050-91fe-d1797af7d489?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in a weekend explosion at a military barracks in Viacha, near La Paz, while an unspecified number remain missing.
* President Rodrigo Paz said the blast appeared to be an accident caused by the improper handling of explosives stored at the facility, though an investigation is continuing.

* **IAEA says Syrian reactor was designed to produce material for nuclear weapons:** International Atomic Energy Agency Director General Rafael Grossi said a North Korean-built reactor in the Syrian city of Deir Az Zor had been [configured](https://substack.com/redirect/f20ec093-7362-4cfa-a7f4-a9efad319c54?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to efficiently produce fissile material that could be used directly in nuclear weapons.
* Israel destroyed the undeclared facility in a 2007 airstrike, after which Bashar al-Assad's government leveled the site and reportedly failed to answer the UN watchdog's questions.
* Invited by Syria's new authorities, Grossi said that IAEA inspectors returned in August and uncovered concealed nuclear material by breaking through walls and navigating narrow passages. The material is now under IAEA safeguards and inspectors are also examining a fuel-fabrication plant, a nuclear-fuel storage facility, and another previously undeclared location.

* **Cuba says talks with Washington have ended over blockade:** Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez said Havana is not [negotiating](https://substack.com/redirect/5f123fc7-1f1e-491b-b654-12ae04d5861c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with the United States and has no agenda for future talks, though diplomatic contacts remain open amid an ongoing U.S. blockade on the country.
* Cuba estimates that the U.S. embargo caused a record $8.1 billion in losses between March 2025 and February 2026--up 7% from the previous period--and says that figure excludes Washington's more recent energy restrictions and secondary sanctions.[ Reuters](https://substack.com/redirect/f180b951-e929-4f0d-83ea-84e36aea7065?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* Rodriguez described the policy as "collective punishment," saying Cubans have endured months with only two or three hours of electricity a day or less, disrupting refrigeration, schools, internet access and family life.
* The dispute will move to the UN General Assembly on October 27-28, when member states are expected to vote again on Cuba's annual resolution demanding an end to the embargo.
* **Kenya offers amnesty to undocumented East Africans amid crackdown fears** : Kenya's government [offered](https://substack.com/redirect/5e6445ee-493a-4906-a535-fef4bea9ae31?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a temporary registration amnesty to undocumented East African nationals Monday after hundreds of Burundians flocked to their embassy in Nairobi, with the refugees fearing a crackdown on small-scale foreign traders. There are roughly 16,000 Burundian refugees and asylum seekers in Kenya, many working in small businesses selling coffee and used clothes.
* Kenyan President William Ruto called on authorities last week to close all foreign-operated small businesses starting Monday following a meeting with Kenyan traders who had protested his tax reforms.
* A spokesperson for Ruto's administration said the government maintains "absolute zero tolerance toward any form of harassment, intimidation, or xenophobia" and that those registering during the amnesty window "will be presumed legally present."

Tuesday, September 8, 2026 -** Russia, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and China push for renewed U.S.-Iran diplomacy; Tehran demands return to MOU. Iran hikes gas prices for heaviest consumers. Amnesty: U.S.-Israeli attacks on Tehran in March may amount to war crimes. Iranian Basij commander killed in "terrorist attack." Elderly Palestinian man injured by Israeli fire in Gaza; Israel issues forced displacement orders. Israeli forces kill four Palestinians, carry out raids and closures across occupied West Bank. UK announces ban on Israeli settlement goods; France and Canada to follow. Haaretz: UAE warned Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu before Oct. 7, but Netanyahu didn't tell security chiefs. Yemeni Saudi-backed forces launch attacks on Ansarallah positions, vow to retake Sana'a. Ansarallah attacks injure 73; hit Saudi energy facilities. Report: Yemen clashes displace 18,500. Israeli attacks kill 12 in southern Lebanon as attacks continue despite "ceasefire." Socialist wave headed for Providence. New Hampshire Senate, House primaries Tuesday. Armed man attacks Ohio gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton. Canada's retaliatory tariffs on $20 billion of U.S. goods take effect. New York residents misled about air quality following 9/11, documents show. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani creates Mayor's Office of Worker Power to boost labor organizing. ICE granted permission to force-feed Cuban detainee via surgical stomach tube. U.S. forces raid vessel in Eastern Pacific and detain crew. Far-right Alternative fur Deutschland party wins state election in eastern Germany. Nine killed in explosion at Bolivian military base. International Atomic Energy Agency says Syrian reactor was designed to produce material for nuclear weapons. Cuba says talks with Washington have ended over blockade. Kenya offers amnesty to undocumented East Africans amid crackdown fears. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran Russia, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and China push for renewed U.S.-Iran diplomacy; Tehran demands return to MOU: Russia and Saudi Arabia are seeking "compromise solutions" to implement the memorandum of understanding between the U.S. and Iran, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said on Tuesday after talks with his Saudi counterpart, Prince Faisal bin Farhan. Lavrov said the two countries "regret" that Arab states have been "dragged against their will" into the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran. Separately, Qatar said it is working with China and other countries to revive U.S.-Iran talks. Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi said the Gulf conflict is threatening regional security and disrupting energy markets, shipping and supply chains. "Pressure through guns and cannons is not the way out. Dialogue and negotiation are the right path," Wang said. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, meanwhile, blamed Washington's "regrettable" violation of the MOU. "The solution is simple; the return and adherence of the American side to its commitments and signing of the memorandum of understanding will pave the way for a return to normalcy," Araghchi . Iran hikes gas prices for heaviest consumers: Iran introduced a price hike for its heaviest gasoline users, according to state media, as the economy continues to suffer as a result of the U.S. blockade, the second such increase since December. Under the new regulations, people buying more than their quota of 110 liters (29 gallons) of gas a month--roughly 15% of consumers--must now pay twice as much. Amnesty: U.S.-Israeli attacks on Tehran in March may amount to war crimes: U.S.-Israeli attacks on three neighborhoods in Tehran in March that killed and wounded dozens of civilians may amount to war crimes, according to a new by Amnesty International. The investigation into air strikes on Niloofar, Resalat, and Javadieh neighborhoods in Tehran between March 1 and 13, 2026 found evidence that "explosive weapons with wide area effects were used in densely populated areas, killing and injuring civilians" and causing widespread and extensive damage to homes. "The civilian death toll, the scale of destruction, the timing of the attacks, the impact on nearby civilian structures and the lack of effective advance warnings point to alarming failures by the U.S.-Israeli coalition...to minimize civilian harm and spare civilian objects," Agnes Callamard, Secretary General of Amnesty International, said in a statement. "The U.S./Israeli strikes in Teheran investigated by Amnesty International, may constitute indiscriminate attacks and amount to war crimes." Drop Site covered two of the three March attacks investigated in the Amnesty investigation. Read our reports on the U.S.-Israeli bombings of and . Iranian Basij commander killed in "terrorist attack": Abdolrauf Eshaghi, a commander in Iran's paramilitary Basij forces, was killed in an attack on Tuesday, according to Iranian state media. Authorities described the incident as a "terrorist attack," but it was not immediately clear who was responsible. Palestine Elderly Palestinian man injured by Israeli fire in Gaza; Israel issues forced displacement orders: Israeli forces an elderly Palestinian man south of Khan Younis on Tuesday, Al Jazeera reported. Since Tuesday morning, Israeli forces have issued at least five forced displacement orders across Gaza. Orders were reported in Al-Bureij, Nuseirat, Gaza City near Al-Shifa Hospital, and at two locations in Al-Shati refugee camp. One of the warned sites, a home near Al-Shifa Hospital, was subsequently hit with three missiles. Israeli forces kill four Palestinians, carry out raids and closures across occupied West Bank: In the past 24 hours, Israeli forces four Palestinians in Qalqilya, Nablus, and Tulkarem governorates, bringing the number of Palestinians killed in the occupied West Bank since the start of the year to 100, according to the Palestinian Health Ministry. Bethlehem: Israeli forces detained two Palestinian teens during a raid in central Bethlehem, according to WAFA. Soldiers also assaulted and injured one of the boys' mothers. Nablus: An Israeli settler was reportedly stabbed multiple times near Aqraba. Israeli forces subsequently closed all entrances to Aqraba and neighboring villages and launched a search for the suspect. UK announces ban on Israeli settlement goods; France and Canada to follow: The UK a ban on trade in goods produced in illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank and sanctions targeting individuals and companies involved in settlement expansion on Tuesday, with Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband calling the move "the beginning of a new approach, to call out injustice and to act." He added, "The British government agrees that there is ethnic cleansing of Palestinians in areas of the West Bank, perpetrated by settler terrorists." In a , the British Palestinian Committee said, "Today's announcement, while welcome, will ultimately be judged not by its rhetoric, but by its enforcement both within and beyond this current government." According to , British diplomats "privately told the US that the sanctions are largely symbolic and will have no material impact on the UK's wider relationship with Israel on trade or security, in a bid to soothe the Trump administration's response." Reuters that the impact of the policy move on bilateral trade with Israel is "likely to be minimal, with details unclear of how the UK will differentiate between goods originating in West Bank settlements [and] products made in Israel." France said it would begin its own process to ban settlement products, while Canada is also expected to join the action. "Why are we doing this? Because the West Bank is close to exploding," French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot on X, continuing, "there is frenzied expansion of the settlements, a flare-up of violence against Palestinians by extremist settlers, and acts of terror which have been attacked by Israeli authorities themselves." Haaretz: UAE warned Netanyahu before Oct. 7, but Netanyahu didn 't tell security chiefs: UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed personally Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in a 45-minute call roughly a week and a half before October 7, 2023, that Hamas leader Yahya Sinwar was planning a major operation, according to a Haaretz investigation. Netanyahu reportedly reacted calmly, insisted Hamas intended to strike the West Bank, and never briefed the heads of Shin Bet, Mossad, or the IDF about the warning. In the months preceding MBZ's warning, Hamas leadership reportedly indicated that it was planning an operation, using a secret backchannel for discussions (through a Fatah intermediary) to warn Israel of a coming "zilzal," or earthquake. That message reached the Shin Bet on September 15 and prompted a security meeting, though no action was taken. Former Shin Bet chief Ronen Bar and former IDF Chief of Staff Herzl Halevi both said they were never informed of MBZ's warning. Bin Zayed did not respond to Haaretz's request for comment. Yemen Yemeni Saudi-backed forces launch attacks on Ansarallah positions, vow to retake Sana 'a: Forces aligned with Yemen's Saudi-backed government launched attacks against Ansarallah positions, as Deputy Defense Minister Samir Al-Sabri said "the decision has been made to retake Sana'a." Fighting intensified in Al-Bayda and Al-Jawf governorates, which lie on routes towards the Ansarallah-held capital. Ansarallah said seven people were killed in a strike on a prison in Al-Hazm, Al-Jawf. Ansarallah attacks injure 73; hit Saudi energy facilities: The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen recent Ansarallah attacks on Saudi Arabia injured 73 people, including women and children. Coalition spokesperson Turki Al-Maliki said its forces would take measures to "deter" Ansarallah and counter further threats. Separately, Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry several energy facilities in the south were hit on Tuesday, causing injuries and fires and temporarily disrupting operations at some sites. Satellite imagery showed plumes of smoke rising from Aramco's Jizan refinery. Report: Yemen clashes displace 18,500: Renewed fighting across Yemen's Taiz and Hodeidah governorates about 18,500 people since hostilities escalated on September 3 with the number "increasing by the hour," according to the International Organization for Migration (IOM), putting further pressure on already overstretched communities in southern Taiz and along the west coast. "Families are arriving with nothing: no shelter, no food, no way to know if it's safe to go back," IOM Yemen chief Abdusattor Esoev said, noting that many have been displaced multiple times. The agency said ongoing clashes and disrupted telecommunications are hampering aid access, while emergency food and shelter stocks have been severely depleted by recent flood responses. Lebanon Israeli attacks kill 12 in southern Lebanon as attacks continue despite "ceasefire": In Kfar Remman, an Israeli airstrike after midnight Monday destroyed a three-story residential building killing 11 members of the same family, including two children and four women, and wounded eight others. An Israeli drone also struck a vehicle in Kfar Remman, killing one paramedic from the Islamic Risala Scout Association and wounding two others. Israeli forces raided Kfarchouba at dawn and raised an Israeli flag on one of the surrounding hills in the Hasbaya district, according to Lebanon 24. Israeli attacks killed 4,381 people and wounded 12,402 between March 2 and September 7, according to Lebanon's Health Ministry. U.S. News Socialist wave headed for Providence: State Rep. David Morales is threatening to become the third socialist to sweep into power in an American city this year, after New York City and Seattle. Incumbent Mayor Brett Smiley trailed the Bernie Sanders -backed Morales in the most recent survey, sponsored by an ally of Morales. The local DSA has not endorsed fellow DSA member Morales; their bylaws ban them from endorsing a candidate running as a Democrat. A November ballot initiative has featured prominently in the race. The measure does not mention Israel but would bar the city from making investments in "foreign countries conducting ethnic cleansing, apartheid, illegal military occupation or genocide." launched a campaign in opposition to the referendum; Mayor Smiley opposes it, while Morales supports it. The race has otherwise played out along familiar lines, with Morales backing off his previous pledges to "defund the police" while promising to focus on making Providence more affordable for working people, while Smiley has maintained the support of the city's landlords, developers, and major business owners. . New Hampshire Senate, House primaries Tuesday: In the Senate primary, insurgent challenger Karishma Manzur , assassinated after helping win the nation's independence, is challenging Rep. Chris Pappas , who is facing a closer-than-expected contest as Manzur has highlighted her opposition to genocide and aligned herself with the Mamdani wing of the party. A recent internal Pappas poll had him ahead by more than 50 points, but a University of New Hampshire survey found Manzur behind by just 13 points. In the race to replace Pappas, two center-left candidates, including the daughter of Sen. Jeanne Shaheen , are leading in polls. Armed man attacks Ohio gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton: An armed individual Ohio Democratic gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton on Sunday at the Canfield Fair near Youngstown, according to her campaign and the state highway patrol, though Acton was not harmed in the incident. The suspect, 38-year-old Patrick Havas, knocked over multiple people while trying to reach Acton and was carrying a taser and two pistols. Police charged him with disorderly conduct and two counts of assault. Canada 's retaliatory tariffs on $20 billion of U.S. goods take effect: New Canadian tariffs on roughly $20 billion in U.S. imports, including clothing, cheese, metal parts, and wood products, took effect Tuesday, mirroring earlier U.S. duties imposed after trade talks between the two countries collapsed last month. Hours before the tariffs took effect, President Donald Trump attacked Canadian plane maker Bombardier on social media, declaring "NO MORE SELLING BOMBARDIER IN THE UNITED STATES!" Bombardier noted in response that it employs "tens of thousands" of American workers and manufactures wings in California and Texas. A new round of U.S. tariffs on additional countries is expected as soon as this week. The Supreme Court previously struck down Trump's duties in February. New York residents misled about air quality following 9/11, documents show: New York City officials evidence of asbestos and other contaminants in Lower Manhattan for months after the September 11 attacks, even as the city publicly assured residents the air was safe, according to 170,000 pages of previously hidden air quality reports and internal correspondence released by Tuesday. The documents were discovered last year and released by Mayor Zohran Mamdani to coincide with the attacks' 25th anniversary. Rep.Jerrold Nadler, whose district included the World Trade Center, said of the Giuliani and Bloomberg administrations, "they knew about the air quality, and they essentially did nothing about it... I suspect that all they cared about was getting Wall Street reopened." Mamdani creates Mayor 's Office of Worker Power to boost labor organizing: Mamdani signed an executive order on Monday creating an Office of Worker Power to support private-sector labor organizing in New York City. The office will be led by Tony Perlstein , a former UAW organizing director, who said its goal is to help workers "stand up and speak up" against wealthy employers who can "afford to pay their workers more." Deputy Mayor for Economic Justice Julie Su , to whom Perlstein will report, clarified that the office "will not be directly going into workplaces and organizing workers" but instead will hold hearings, share information on worker rights, and refer participants to unions and worker centers. ICE granted permission to force-feed Cuban detainee via surgical stomach tube : A federal judge in Texas ICE's request to force-feed a Cuban hunger striker held at the privately run Montgomery ICE processing center, including through a rare, nonconsensual surgical procedure involving a permanent gastric feeding tube, according to court records reported on by The Guardian. Judge Andrew Hanen initially authorized the force-feeding on August 19 and extended the order this week, though DHS said Thursday the man had "resumed eating and drinking again" and was not currently being force-fed. The man, arrested by ICE on July 22 and declared a hunger striker three days later, lacks legal representation. Since January 2025, the agency has received court approval at least 19 times for involuntary medical procedures on hunger strikers. U.S. forces raid vessel in Eastern Pacific and detain crew: U.S. forces raided a vessel in the Eastern Pacific on Monday, detaining everyone on board, to U.S. Southern Command (SOUTHCOM), which posted a video of the attack and saying the vessel was "supporting illicit at-sea drug trafficking" without providing evidence. "After clearing the vessel and disembarking the crew, U.S. forces sank it," SOUTHCOM said. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Far-right AfD party wins state election in eastern Germany: The Alternative for Germany party elections in Germany's Saxony-Anhalt state while securing 39 of 83 seats, leaving it three short of a governing majority. If the AfD succeeds in forming a government, it would become the first far-right party to control a German state since World War II, gaining authority over areas including policing, education, and culture. Several parties ruled out cooperation with the AfD, raising the possibility of a minority government, defections from other parties, or another election. The AfD's state branch is officially classified as a right-wing extremist organization by Germany's domestic intelligence and the party has been criticized within Germany for alleged support for Russia. Nine killed in explosion at Bolivian military base: Bolivian authorities said that nine people were in a weekend explosion at a military barracks in Viacha, near La Paz, while an unspecified number remain missing. President Rodrigo Paz said the blast appeared to be an accident caused by the improper handling of explosives stored at the facility, though an investigation is continuing. IAEA says Syrian reactor was designed to produce material for nuclear weapons: International Atomic Energy Agency Director General Rafael Grossi said a North Korean-built reactor in the Syrian city of Deir Az Zor had been to efficiently produce fissile material that could be used directly in nuclear weapons. Israel destroyed the undeclared facility in a 2007 airstrike, after which Bashar al-Assad's government leveled the site and reportedly failed to answer the UN watchdog's questions. Invited by Syria's new authorities, Grossi said that IAEA inspectors returned in August and uncovered concealed nuclear material by breaking through walls and navigating narrow passages. The material is now under IAEA safeguards and inspectors are also examining a fuel-fabrication plant, a nuclear-fuel storage facility, and another previously undeclared location. Cuba says talks with Washington have ended over blockade: Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez said Havana is not with the United States and has no agenda for future talks, though diplomatic contacts remain open amid an ongoing U.S. blockade on the country. Cuba estimates that the U.S. embargo caused a record $8.1 billion in losses between March 2025 and February 2026--up 7% from the previous period--and says that figure excludes Washington's more recent energy restrictions and secondary sanctions. Rodriguez described the policy as "collective punishment," saying Cubans have endured months with only two or three hours of electricity a day or less, disrupting refrigeration, schools, internet access and family life. The dispute will move to the UN General Assembly on October 27-28, when member states are expected to vote again on Cuba's annual resolution demanding an end to the embargo. Kenya offers amnesty to undocumented East Africans amid crackdown fears : Kenya's government a temporary registration amnesty to undocumented East African nationals Monday after hundreds of Burundians flocked to their embassy in Nairobi, with the refugees fearing a crackdown on small-scale foreign traders. There are roughly 16,000 Burundian refugees and asylum seekers in Kenya, many working in small businesses selling coffee and used clothes. Kenyan President William Ruto called on authorities last week to close all foreign-operated small businesses starting Monday following a meeting with Kenyan traders who had protested his tax reforms. **Medicare’s Hospital Markup Is Costing Seniors** By Bobby Jindal and Charlie Katebi
---
Medicare pays hospital-owned clinics up to 670 percent more than independent physician offices for the exact same care. In early July, the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) proposed ending that markup for common imaging services without contrast, including X-rays, MRIs and ultrasounds, by paying certain hospital-owned clinics the same rates as independent physician offices. The reform would lower costs for America’s seniors while saving beneficiaries and taxpayers $260 million in 2027 and $7.2 billion over the next 10 years. Seniors and taxpayers should cheer for this proposal and demand Washington go even further. Under Medicare’s current rules, the same medical service can cost dramatically more simply because it is provided in a hospital-owned clinic. In that setting, Medicare sends two payments: a payment to the doctor and a facility fee to the hospital that owns the practice. As a result, Medicare can pay hospital-owned facilities 43 percent to 670 percent more than independent practices for identical services. Seniors pay for this markup directly, as Medicare beneficiaries pay a 20 percent coinsurance for outpatient care. In 2023, for example, an epidural injection would cost a senior $148.17 in coinsurance at a hospital-owned clinic, compared with just $51.17 at a freestanding physician's office.

disclaimer_text: Paid for by Sara Jacobs for Congress
body:
| | | |
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138795511/645233787/-642992695?amount=25&refcode=260908em_sjj_press&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84OTMxMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4MzFlMmRlNy1hMmFiLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=gcRd6US89SiEKMqOHXMwhwRai9hbAP4A7g_gLaMz6_8=)
---
You’ve probably seen the insane back and forth over the past year between Pete Hegseth and the journalists who cover the Pentagon. If you haven’t, the gist of it is that Hegseth doesn’t want any real, factual coverage of his work at the Department of Defense, and he’s going to great lengths to restrict the freedom of the press.
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138795512/645233789/1892458971?refcode=260908em_sjj_press&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84OTMxMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4MzFlMmRlNy1hMmFiLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=gcRd6US89SiEKMqOHXMwhwRai9hbAP4A7g_gLaMz6_8=&emci=fb304adb-9cab-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&emdi=831e2de7-a2ab-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=14239920)
---
**His posture towards the press and his attempts to come between journalists and their jobs is out of control, so I just introduced new legislation called The Protecting Pentagon Press Access Act.**[**Learn more and add your name to support my legislation right here.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138795514/645233790/1892458971?refcode=260908em_sjj_press&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84OTMxMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4MzFlMmRlNy1hMmFiLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=gcRd6US89SiEKMqOHXMwhwRai9hbAP4A7g_gLaMz6_8=&emci=fb304adb-9cab-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&emdi=831e2de7-a2ab-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=14239920) Let’s back up for a second and talk about how we got here: **First** , last fall, Hegseth kicked NBC News, NPR, the New York Times, and CNN out of their dedicated workspaces and replaced them with pro-Trump outlets that had never covered the Pentagon a day in their lives. **Then,** he shut down the briefing room, banned reporters from entire wings of the building, and tried to make journalists sign a loyalty pledge as a condition of doing their jobs. **Now,** the Pentagon declared its own press office a classified space. Which, for the record, it is not! **For an administration that talks a big game about loving the First Amendment, these guys sure do hate freedom of the press!** _But this is more than just garden variety hypocrisy. If you take the press out of the Pentagon, you blind the American people to what’s happening in their name and with their tax dollars._ It's because of CNN that we know about the initial U.S. drone strikes on Venezuelan soil. It's because of NPR that we know about the strikes on the girls' elementary school in Minab, Iran — where more than 175 students and teachers were killed — and it's because of Reuters that we know the Pentagon's own inquiry pointed to the U.S. being at fault. And not for nothing, it's because of CBS News that we learned Secretary Hegseth wanted a makeup studio at the Pentagon. Hegseth will claim his restriction of the press is about security (which is rich, coming from the same guy who recklessly shared sensitive operational details on an unclassified messaging app). But we know better: it’s about hiding the truth, and it’s about controlling the media. **We can’t let that happen, so we’re taking action. My new bill was introduced in partnership with Rep. Don Bacon, a Republican — because the First Amendment isn’t a partisan issue — and would make sure credentialed journalists get the access they need to the Pentagon, without loyalty pledges, political litmus tests, or retaliation for tough coverage.** **[Will you sign my petition today to support the Protecting Pentagon Press Act, stand up for the freedom of the press, and demand accountability at Hegseth’s Pentagon?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138795516/645233791/1892458971?refcode=260908em_sjj_press&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84OTMxMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4MzFlMmRlNy1hMmFiLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=gcRd6US89SiEKMqOHXMwhwRai9hbAP4A7g_gLaMz6_8=&emci=fb304adb-9cab-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&emdi=831e2de7-a2ab-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=14239920)**
---
[ **SIGN THE PETITION** ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138795518/645233794/1892458971?refcode=260908em_sjj_press&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84OTMxMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4MzFlMmRlNy1hMmFiLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=gcRd6US89SiEKMqOHXMwhwRai9hbAP4A7g_gLaMz6_8=&emci=fb304adb-9cab-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&emdi=831e2de7-a2ab-f111-9b33-0022482a933b&ceid=14239920)
---
Every administration, both Democratic and Republican, has upheld these basic standards for half a century without needing a legal mandate to do so — but as we know all too well by now, the Trump administration is not normal, and will _not_ uphold democratic standards unless we make them. That’s what I’m working towards with this legislation, and it’s what I’ll keep doing every single day until we kick them out of power. Thanks for reading and for being on this team! —Sara

clean_body: | | | | = You’ve probably seen the insane back and forth over the past year between Pete Hegseth and the journalists who cover the Pentagon. If you haven’t, the gist of it is that Hegseth doesn’t want any real, factual coverage of his work at the Department of Defense, and he’s going to great lengths to restrict the freedom of the press. His posture towards the press and his attempts to come between journalists and their jobs is out of control, so I just introduced new legislation called The Protecting Pentagon Press Access Act. Let’s back up for a second and talk about how we got here: First , last fall, Hegseth kicked NBC News, NPR, the New York Times, and CNN out of their dedicated workspaces and replaced them with pro-Trump outlets that had never covered the Pentagon a day in their lives. Then, he shut down the briefing room, banned reporters from entire wings of the building, and tried to make journalists sign a loyalty pledge as a condition of doing their jobs. Now, the Pentagon declared its own press office a classified space. Which, for the record, it is not! For an administration that talks a big game about loving the First Amendment, these guys sure do hate freedom of the press! But this is more than just garden variety hypocrisy. If you take the press out of the Pentagon, you blind the American people to what’s happening in their name and with their tax dollars. It's because of CNN that we know about the initial U.S. drone strikes on Venezuelan soil. It's because of NPR that we know about the strikes on the girls' elementary school in Minab, Iran — where more than 175 students and teachers were killed — and it's because of Reuters that we know the Pentagon's own inquiry pointed to the U.S. being at fault. And not for nothing, it's because of CBS News that we learned Secretary Hegseth wanted a makeup studio at the Pentagon. Hegseth will claim his restriction of the press is about security (which is rich, coming from the same guy who recklessly shared sensitive operational details on an unclassified messaging app). But we know better: it’s about hiding the truth, and it’s about controlling the media. We can’t let that happen, so we’re taking action. My new bill was introduced in partnership with Rep. Don Bacon, a Republican — because the First Amendment isn’t a partisan issue — and would make sure credentialed journalists get the access they need to the Pentagon, without loyalty pledges, political litmus tests, or retaliation for tough coverage. Every administration, both Democratic and Republican, has upheld these basic standards for half a century without needing a legal mandate to do so — but as we know all too well by now, the Trump administration is not normal, and will not uphold democratic standards unless we make them. That’s what I’m working towards with this legislation, and it’s what I’ll keep doing every single day until we kick them out of power. Thanks for reading and for being on this team! —Sara = | | | Congresswoman Sara JacobsCalifornia’s 51st District = | = Paid for by Sara Jacobs for Congress Sara Jacobs for Congress PO Box 120085 San Diego, CA 92112 United States | | | | | | ---|---|--- We believe these emails are a critical way for Sara to stay in touch with supporters and constituents. | | Dear Fellow American, **Is human nature fixed, or can it be changed?** That question lies at the heart of some of the most consequential ideas in history. Karl Marx believed that if society could be upended, mankind itself could be remade. That promise inspired revolutionary movements throughout the twentieth century--with catastrophic consequences, as communist regimes claimed the lives of more than 100 million people. **Sadly, we 're seeing a resurgence of this destructive ideology right here in the United States.** But anyone who's read Homer understands something far different. Nearly **3,000 years ago** , _The Iliad_ portrayed men and women with the same hopes, fears, loves, jealousies, ambitions, courage, and grief that we recognize today. Open its pages, and you discover something remarkable: **Human nature has not changed.** Near the end of the poem, King Priam of Troy enters the camp of Achilles, the warrior who killed his beloved son Hector. The old king kneels before his enemy and begs for his son's body. Achilles thinks of his own aging father, and both men weep together. Every parent understands that scene. Every son can understand it. Across three millennia, Homer reminds us that what is deepest in human nature remains the same. That is why _The Iliad_ has endured as one of the foundational works of Western civilization. And it is one reason Hillsdale College created our free online course, **" The Iliad."** The course introduces students to truths about courage, honor, sacrifice, friendship, justice, and duty--truths that every generation must rediscover if liberty is to endure. Those same truths also expose the false promise behind every utopian ideology: **that human nature can somehow be perfected simply by changing politics or economics.** **Will you make a tax-deductible gift today to help us introduce 100,000 Americans to these timeless lessons through Hillsdale 's free online course on _The Iliad_?** Will you help? Howdy, folks, it’s John here! I was looking through some old photos and wanted to share some with you.

Howdy, folks, it’s John here! I was looking through some old photos and wanted to share some with you. ([Then, we hope you’ll donate to help us keep Colorado blue!](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138795638/645234193/927086807?refcode=email_090826_mystory&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83MjY1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmNTdhY2MzZS1hM2FiLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=_nDNAqMX2FFLkc8CgeaZqhdSfMdjUDhyRKYsFJKHAjc=)) As a kid, I was never the strongest, the fastest — or heck, even the smartest kid on the playground. But I learned something important: Through determination, hard work, and perseverance, any challenge can be overcome. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138795639/645234194/927086807?refcode=email_090826_mystory&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83MjY1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmNTdhY2MzZS1hM2FiLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=_nDNAqMX2FFLkc8CgeaZqhdSfMdjUDhyRKYsFJKHAjc=) I never imagined I’d end up in politics. In those early days, I studied science and began my career as a geologist. That is, until the company I worked for was bought, and I was laid off for 27 months. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138795640/645234195/927086807?refcode=email_090826_mystory&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83MjY1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmNTdhY2MzZS1hM2FiLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=_nDNAqMX2FFLkc8CgeaZqhdSfMdjUDhyRKYsFJKHAjc=) Eventually, I decided to take a gamble. I took every scrap of savings in my bank account and opened my own business, Wynkoop Brewing Company, in downtown Denver. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138795641/645234196/927086807?refcode=email_090826_mystory&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83MjY1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmNTdhY2MzZS1hM2FiLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=_nDNAqMX2FFLkc8CgeaZqhdSfMdjUDhyRKYsFJKHAjc=) I loved the Wynkoop — and loved not having a boss. But as time went on, I saw firsthand just how often the government seemed to work against the little guy — working people and small business owners like me. So I took a leap of faith and ran for Mayor of Denver to fix that. I never even ran for student council before! _And we won._ [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138795642/645234197/927086807?refcode=email_090826_mystory&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83MjY1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmNTdhY2MzZS1hM2FiLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=_nDNAqMX2FFLkc8CgeaZqhdSfMdjUDhyRKYsFJKHAjc=) Then, I went on to serve two terms as Governor of Colorado, always focusing on putting Colorado families first. In 2020, we took that same spirit and, with the help of folks like you, flipped Colorado’s Senate seat blue. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138795643/645234198/927086807?refcode=email_090826_mystory&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83MjY1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmNTdhY2MzZS1hM2FiLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=_nDNAqMX2FFLkc8CgeaZqhdSfMdjUDhyRKYsFJKHAjc=) Since then, we’ve worked to deliver real results for working families. From passing legislation to lower housing costs to addressing climate change head-on. But with President Trump and his MAGA cronies in full control in Washington, our progress is under attack. ## **Don 't Play Defense: Why the Media's Attacks on JD Vance Keep Backfiring**
The mainstream media isn't running a news cycle on JD Vance - they're running a trap.
The problem for them is that Vance refuses to fall into it.
If you turned on cable news or opened a major newspaper this week, you saw the exact same playbook on full display during JD Vance's White House press briefing.
The press sets up loaded, hostile questions, expecting the politician to stumble into a defensive apology.
Instead, Vance walks right up to the briefing room podium, confronts the bias head-on, and dismantles the premise of their setup in real time.
His rapid-fire answers at this week's White House briefing speak for themselves:
[| | | | | Daily Signal
---
@DailySignal
JD VANCE: Midterm Elections Are Between 'Common Sense' and 'Crazy' "Do you want to live in a country that has safety and security and prosperity? If the answer is yes, and I think most Americans do, then vote for congressional Republicans over congressional Democrats. On every ...

When you turn on the news this week, don't just watch what the press asks.

clean_body: The special and the runoff took everything we had. November is less than 70 days away. | Peter - I'm going to be straight with you, because that's the only way I know how to do this. We just won. Two elections in two weeks: the special primary, then the runoff. Grueling doesn't begin to cover it. Every dollar this campaign had went into turning out voters, running ads, and getting our message into every corner of this state. And it worked. But here's the part nobody tells you on election night: winning a runoff doesn't put a single dollar back in our account. Right now, after everything we just spent, our campaign finances are running on fumes. Annie Andrews has $4.1 million. She's raised nearly $11 million since she got into this race, from liberal donors across the country. She's had months to build that war chest while we were fighting a two-round primary just to get our name on the November ballot. Countless conservatives in SC put their trust in me, and I promise to carry forward the conservative agenda for the next six years in the United States Senate. After asking me to run, President Trump stood on stage with me and told you why he trusts me, too. I don't intend to let a bigger bank account decide whether I get to keep that promise. The general election is November 3. That sounds far off. It isn't. It's less than 70 days away. Every week between now and then, Annie Andrews's campaign will be on television, in your mailbox, and on your phone - funded by liberal donors who wanted to defeat Lindsey and now, defeat me. We have to be able to answer that, and right now, we can't. My opponent has a $4 million head start. To catch up and rebuild, I need not only patriots who were with us over the last six weeks, but folks who are stepping up for the first time. Don't let the most radical candidate South Carolina Democrats have nominated buy this seat. Thank you for standing with me, Darline Graham United States Senator P.S. I hope you all had a wonderful Labor Day weekend. I hope you got real time with your friends and your family. I did -- most of mine was in Wisconsin with my people, and it was good.
There was one blip. Work got in the way exactly once, and it came in the form of a prolonged argument with my conspiracy-theory-loving nemesis, Laura Loomer, over her absolutely disgusting attacks on Amy Acton, the Democratic candidate for governor of Ohio.
Here's what happened: A deranged Republican lunatic lunged at Acton while carrying multiple firearms and another weapon on top of that. Several people were hurt. Thankfully, Amy was not.
And here's how I found out about it: I logged onto X in the middle of an otherwise pleasant afternoon (always a mistake) and found Laura Loomer attacking Acton for showing up late to her own event -- blaming the lateness on the bullshit story they have manufactured out of thin air that Amy is some kind of alcoholic. She isn't. It's a lie, and it has always been a lie. A woman almost got killed and their instinct, within minutes, was to run the smear one more time.
* * *
**Today 's rant is sponsored by Ground News.**
Lately, I've found myself asking a simple question when I read the news: _what am I not being shown?_ Not because I'm trying to "both sides" everything--but because outrage is good for clicks, and clarity usually isn't.
That's why I use Ground News--the app and website that gathers over 50,000 new sources worldwide in one place so you can see how the same story is being covered across the political spectrum, for every story you get a visual breakdown of the bias, how reliable the source is and who owns the source reporting.
I'm a paying user and was before they ever sponsored Endless Urgency. I reached out because tools like this make people harder to manipulate--and that matters. If you want a clearer, more complete picture of the news, I genuinely recommend it.
They also highlight stories that are underreported by one side of the political spectrum in their Blindspot Feed. These are stories you could be missing in your media bubble.

* * *
The attacks Loomer has run in coordination with the Ohio Republican Party -- and make no mistake about it, those two are working together, have been vile from the beginning. They've hurled vicious slurs at her. They've lied about her record. They've attacked her for trauma she survived in her own life.
Brick by brick they built a climate where the most unstable person in the room could hear all of it and conclude that Amy Acton was fair game. And in that climate, the brother of a Republican lobbyist -- a lobbyist who previously had to quit his job when it was discovered he was a pedophile -- felt like he could go and do what I believe was an attempted attack on her.
Now Loomer is on X losing her mind, claiming the whole thing was staged. That _we_ staged it.
Staged it to do what, exactly? Amy Acton is the frontrunner to be the next governor of Ohio. Frontrunners don't need to manufacture attempts on their own lives. There is no version of this where the upside is worth it, and everybody knows it.
So I said what I actually think: that it may well have been one of her own people who did this, and that her frantic staging attacks looks an awful lot like overcompensation. That's when she threatened to sue me.
Which brings us back to where we started. I would love it. It would be genuinely hilarious if Laura Loomer, of all people, sued me, of all people. The deposition alone would be worth the legal fees -- sit her down under oath and walk her line by line through everything she's said about Amy Acton, and see how much of it she's willing to repeat with consequences attached. I'll clear my calendar. I'll bring snacks.
Because here's what she can't sue her way out of: whether or not one of her people pulled this, she is complicit in it. She spent months lying about Amy Acton to an audience that includes some of the least stable people in American politics. You don't get to pour gasoline for a month and then act shocked when something catches.
It's just one more reminder that every accusation from the right is a confession. They tell you we stage things because they stage things. That's how they think about their own supporters -- as an audience to be manipulated into sympathy. A lot of people believe what happened at the White House Correspondents' Dinner was staged. I don't know if it was or it wasn't. What I know is that it was weird as hell and I don't buy the story we were handed.
What a sad, miserable excuse for a political party the GOP has become -- one effectively run by Laura Loomer, a close personal adviser to the President of the United States. Trump hasn't said a thing about this. Amy's opponent, Vivek Ramaswamy, couldn't be bothered to put out a statement under his own name; he let his communications director do it for him, and it took roughly twenty-four hours before I saw him on camera saying anything at all. Absolutely disgusting.

* * *
Political violence has gone up over the last ten years and I won't pretend otherwise. Most of that, in my opinion, comes out of economic and political turmoil. Some of it is downstream of Donald Trump. But there are other players here too, including foreign actors who would love nothing more than to keep our government tearing itself apart. I firmly believe there are foreign hands feeding Laura Loomer some of the slop she puts out, and I hope that gets investigated the moment Democrats take back Congress.
Let me end this very messy rant with one thought. In a world full of Vivek Ramaswamys -- do-nothing liars who con people and have no real interest in improving a single life -- be an Amy Acton.
Amy Acton stayed behind to help people who were hurt in an attack aimed at her. She could have run. She could have spent the week manufacturing cheap political moments at her opponent's expense, and nobody would have blamed her. Instead she had a message of unity and safety, and she put it into action by helping people. That's what elected officials are supposed to do -- figure out how to be useful in your community, then go be useful. Instead we've got some of the most corrupt, deranged grifters on the planet, from Trump to Ramaswamy on down through a million candidates up and down the ballot who don't give a damn about you or me. And yes, there are plenty of Democrats like that too. I'm not going to pretend this is a purely partisan disease.
Here's the part that scares me most. When this stuff happens -- the violence, the lies, the smears, the case where a public figure had his kids taken from him because a woman lied and said he'd abused them, because she didn't like his politics -- it makes good people less likely to run for office. That's not a side effect.
But the only way out is through. We need good people to run. We need _you_ to run, or organize, or get involved however you can, because we cannot keep handing this country to the worst among us. Somebody has to take the plunge and dive off the deep end with the rest of us, even though it's terrifying. That's the only way we ever cut this malignant tumor out of American life.
With urgency,
--Mike

clean_body: Please do. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more ? Please do. | | | Sep 8 | | | | | | | | | | | | I hope you all had a wonderful Labor Day weekend. I hope you got real time with your friends and your family. I did -- most of mine was in Wisconsin with my people, and it was good. There was one blip. Work got in the way exactly once, and it came in the form of a prolonged argument with my conspiracy-theory-loving nemesis, Laura Loomer, over her absolutely disgusting attacks on Amy Acton, the Democratic candidate for governor of Ohio. Here's what happened: A deranged Republican lunatic lunged at Acton while carrying multiple firearms and another weapon on top of that. Several people were hurt. Thankfully, Amy was not. And here's how I found out about it: I logged onto X in the middle of an otherwise pleasant afternoon (always a mistake) and found Laura Loomer attacking Acton for showing up late to her own event -- blaming the lateness on the bullshit story they have manufactured out of thin air that Amy is some kind of alcoholic. She isn't. It's a lie, and it has always been a lie. A woman almost got killed and their instinct, within minutes, was to run the smear one more time. Today 's rant is sponsored by Ground News. Lately, I've found myself asking a simple question when I read the news: what am I not being shown? Not because I'm trying to "both sides" everything--but because outrage is good for clicks, and clarity usually isn't. That's why I use Ground News--the app and website that gathers over 50,000 new sources worldwide in one place so you can see how the same story is being covered across the political spectrum, for every story you get a visual breakdown of the bias, how reliable the source is and who owns the source reporting. I'm a paying user and was before they ever sponsored Endless Urgency. I reached out because tools like this make people harder to manipulate--and that matters. If you want a clearer, more complete picture of the news, I genuinely recommend it. They also highlight stories that are underreported by one side of the political spectrum in their Blindspot Feed. These are stories you could be missing in your media bubble. See every side of every story with Ground News. Subscribe through my link for 40% off their unlimited access Vantage Plan -> | | ---|---|--- The attacks Loomer has run in coordination with the Ohio Republican Party -- and make no mistake about it, those two are working together, have been vile from the beginning. They've hurled vicious slurs at her. They've lied about her record. They've attacked her for trauma she survived in her own life. Brick by brick they built a climate where the most unstable person in the room could hear all of it and conclude that Amy Acton was fair game. And in that climate, the brother of a Republican lobbyist -- a lobbyist who previously had to quit his job when it was discovered he was a pedophile -- felt like he could go and do what I believe was an attempted attack on her. Now Loomer is on X losing her mind, claiming the whole thing was staged. That we staged it. Staged it to do what, exactly? Amy Acton is the frontrunner to be the next governor of Ohio. Frontrunners don't need to manufacture attempts on their own lives. There is no version of this where the upside is worth it, and everybody knows it. So I said what I actually think: that it may well have been one of her own people who did this, and that her frantic staging attacks looks an awful lot like overcompensation. That's when she threatened to sue me. Which brings us back to where we started. I would love it. It would be genuinely hilarious if Laura Loomer, of all people, sued me, of all people. The deposition alone would be worth the legal fees -- sit her down under oath and walk her line by line through everything she's said about Amy Acton, and see how much of it she's willing to repeat with consequences attached. I'll clear my calendar. I'll bring snacks. Because here's what she can't sue her way out of: whether or not one of her people pulled this, she is complicit in it. She spent months lying about Amy Acton to an audience that includes some of the least stable people in American politics. You don't get to pour gasoline for a month and then act shocked when something catches. It's just one more reminder that every accusation from the right is a confession. They tell you we stage things because they stage things. That's how they think about their own supporters -- as an audience to be manipulated into sympathy. A lot of people believe what happened at the White House Correspondents' Dinner was staged. I don't know if it was or it wasn't. What I know is that it was weird as hell and I don't buy the story we were handed. What a sad, miserable excuse for a political party the GOP has become -- one effectively run by Laura Loomer, a close personal adviser to the President of the United States. Trump hasn't said a thing about this. Amy's opponent, Vivek Ramaswamy, couldn't be bothered to put out a statement under his own name; he let his communications director do it for him, and it took roughly twenty-four hours before I saw him on camera saying anything at all. Absolutely disgusting. When a story feels too tidy, I always ask: what 's missing? Ground News shows how the same story is covered across the political spectrum and highlights blind spots most outlets ignore. My team and I use it because context matters. Try it today! Political violence has gone up over the last ten years and I won't pretend otherwise. Most of that, in my opinion, comes out of economic and political turmoil. Some of it is downstream of Donald Trump. But there are other players here too, including foreign actors who would love nothing more than to keep our government tearing itself apart. I firmly believe there are foreign hands feeding Laura Loomer some of the slop she puts out, and I hope that gets investigated the moment Democrats take back Congress. Let me end this very messy rant with one thought. In a world full of Vivek Ramaswamys -- do-nothing liars who con people and have no real interest in improving a single life -- be an Amy Acton. Amy Acton stayed behind to help people who were hurt in an attack aimed at her. She could have run. She could have spent the week manufacturing cheap political moments at her opponent's expense, and nobody would have blamed her. Instead she had a message of unity and safety, and she put it into action by helping people. That's what elected officials are supposed to do -- figure out how to be useful in your community, then go be useful. Instead we've got some of the most corrupt, deranged grifters on the planet, from Trump to Ramaswamy on down through a million candidates up and down the ballot who don't give a damn about you or me. And yes, there are plenty of Democrats like that too. I'm not going to pretend this is a purely partisan disease. Here's the part that scares me most. When this stuff happens -- the violence, the lies, the smears, the case where a public figure had his kids taken from him because a woman lied and said he'd abused them, because she didn't like his politics -- it makes good people less likely to run for office. That's not a side effect. But the only way out is through. We need good people to run. We need you to run, or organize, or get involved however you can, because we cannot keep handing this country to the worst among us. Somebody has to take the plunge and dive off the deep end with the rest of us, even though it's terrifying. That's the only way we ever cut this malignant tumor out of American life. With urgency, --Mike P.S. If you ever read a headline and think "there's more to this than I'm being told," that's exactly why I use Ground News.
