Bangor Savings Bank has moved to foreclose on the Falmouth home of Abdullahi Ali, the Somali-American refugee poster child whose company collected roughly $5 million per year in MaineCare payments before the Maine Wire exposed allegations of systemic fraud and multiple failed audits the state had kept quiet.
Ali's company, Gateway Community Services LLC, and its 501(c)(3) arm, Gateway Community Services Maine, were among the top recipients of Medicaid funding in the state of Maine from 2018 to 2025, according to MaineCare payment records obtained via a Freedom of Access Act request.
In addition, Ali was awarded multiple lucrative no-bid contracts from the Mills administration -- and he received nearly $700,000 from the Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) during the COVID-19 pandemic.
Yet with all that taxpayer money flowing into his bank account, Ali somehow forgot to pay his taxes in 2023 and 2024.
Cumberland County tax lien and foreclosure records filed against the bougie million-dollar home Ali owned in the wealthy suburb of Portland show that the top Democrat activist owes $44,082.54 in back taxes and will no longer be able to sell his house.
A clerk's certificate filed in Cumberland County Superior Court identifies Ali as the defendant and Maine Revenue Services as a party in interest in a case that concerns the Hardy Road property Ali put on the market for $1 million earlier this year, while he was reportedly spending much of his time in Kenya and Dubai.

The Cumberland County records appear to foreshadow a fight between Bangor Savings Bank and the state of Maine over who will get paid back first -- if at all.
It's not clear how the Somali-American refugee was able to continue fraudulently billing Medicaid and receiving no-bid contracts from the Mills administration for several years while failing to pay his own income taxes.

#### [Migrant Agency Accused of MaineCare Fraud Boasts Extensive Ties to Maine Democrats](https://substack.com/redirect/6d72e066-df6a-4f50-9ed8-7088ea9f2a3e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Gov. Janet Mills (D) poses with former Gateway Ass. Exec. Dir. State Rep. Deqa Dhalac, Gateway CEO Abdullahi Ali, and former Gateway employee turned Office of New American's policy analyst Elkhas Ahmed
The foreclosure filing might be the only justice Maine taxpayers get, as no charges have been filed in relation to Gateway Community Services and Ali has refused to return from Africa since the Maine Wire exposed the fraudulent conduct of his business, a so-called "migrant services" agency at the center of the Maine Democratic Party's power structure.
Indeed, rather than file charges in the Gateway case, Maine Attorney General Aaron Frey awarded the migrant agency $400,000 in opioid settlement money last year.
For years, the company received millions of dollars annually through Maine's Medicaid program while Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) auditors continually found the company had overbilled the program. Even though three state audits found Gateway improperly billed MaineCare for more than $1.6 million in services, the state never stopped shoveling money into the agency until the Maine Wire published the audits and whistleblower allegations.
As first reported in March of 2025, Gateway is intricately tied to the Maine Democratic Party: Rep. Deqa Dhalac (D-South Portland) served as an assistant executive director; Rep. Yusuf Yusuf (D-Portland) worked for the company before going on to found his own home health care agency; Ekhlas Ahmed, a former Gateway employee, now works as the "policy analyst" for the Office of New Americans, formed by Gov. Janet Mills but based on a bill from Dhalac; and Safiya Khalid, a Democratic activist in Lewiston, worked as an assistant to Ali before starting Gateway's political arm, the Community Organizing Alliance (COA).
[Share The Robinson Report](https://substack..5yHIAAE1Wh2UT8OvHreRzti7rCCljV9AbaNzdkf6mNI?)
Now Ali faces a bank's attempt to foreclose on his home, with the state's tax collection agency also named in the proceeding.
[The Robinson Report reported in January](https://substack.com/redirect/57b1c57e-8660-4e7e-a0ca-4e1afd6a7fc4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Ali had listed the 3,312-square-foot property for $1 million shortly after Homeland Security Investigations agents appeared at Gateway's Lewiston office.
That report cited Ali's public social media posts placing him largely in Kenya and Dubai following his unsuccessful 2024 campaign for president of Jubaland, a region of Somalia.
Ali's overseas political ambitions helped bring his Maine business dealings under scrutiny.
In March 2025, [The Maine Wire reported](https://substack.com/redirect/e82157c6-1561-457b-87a6-d73d18cb65c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Gateway Community Services LLC had received roughly $5 million per year in MaineCare payments from 2019 through 2025, according to records obtained under a Freedom of Access Act request. During that period, Ali also publicly described helping finance armed forces in Somalia, including purchases of weapons, ammunition and food.
Ali bragged that the militia he was funding -- during a period when we now know he was not paying taxes on the more than $400,000 per year he earned from his government-funded gig -- would be used to topple the sitting president of Jubaland after the 2024 "election."
The scrutiny intensified when former Gateway billing specialist [Christopher Bernardini](https://substack.com/redirect/c71c7a42-1f61-4218-af68-adbdd8e46cfa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) came forward. In allegations [first published in this Substack in May 2025](https://substack.com/redirect/c71c7a42-1f61-4218-af68-adbdd8e46cfa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Bernardini said supervisors fabricated service hours and inflated Medicaid claims at Ali's direction.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/c71c7a42-1f61-4218-af68-adbdd8e46cfa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)| | |
#### [Somali-American Refugee's Medicaid Agency Submitted Bogus MaineCare Claims for Years, Former Employees Allege](https://substack.com/redirect/c71c7a42-1f61-4218-af68-adbdd8e46cfa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/c71c7a42-1f61-4218-af68-adbdd8e46cfa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
According to documents Bernardini provided to The Robinson Report, the former Gateway employee submitted a complaint to Maine State Auditor Matt Dunlap (D) in 2024 to report suspected fraud, but he never heard back from the Office of the State Auditor (OSA).
Dunlap is now the Democratic nominee for Maine's Second Congressional District.
Rather than moving swiftly to investigate and shut down Gateway, Maine Revenue Services sent Bernardini a letter informing him that it was auditing _his_ taxes. Because he had moved to Florida during the Covid-19 shutdowns and Gateway had continued withholding taxes from his paycheck as if he were a Maine resident, the audit process determined that _the state in fact owed Bernardini_ a substantial sum in overpaid taxes.
Bernardini also believes that he was wrongfully terminated from Gateway for blowing the whistle; however, every employment law firm he's approached about suing Gateway for back pay has turned down his case.
"I chose integrity over a cushy job," Bernardini said.
Gateway has denied fraud.
In response to our reporting, Ali called the Maine Wire "racist and hateful" in a post to X.
"I make no apologies for building a successful business in Maine," he said.
DHHS, meanwhile, identified substantial repayment obligations. Two earlier reviews resulted in demands for approximately $125,000 and $537,550 after adjustments. A subsequent audit covering March 2021 through December 2022 identified more than $1 million in additional questioned billings.
On December 23, 2025, the Department of Health and Human Services suspended MaineCare payments to Gateway after determining there was a "credible allegation of fraud." DHHS upheld the suspension in May. Gateway then missed its July 17 deadline to appeal, [The Maine Wire reported](https://substack.com/redirect/e8b1f1c6-fa3c-4caf-8910-b6bd2a57d792?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Now, Maine Revenue Services has identified $44,082.54 in unpaid state income taxes.
Gateway has attributed the disputed billings to documentation deficiencies, changing guidance and administrative errors, as opposed to the intentional fraud alleged by Bernardini.

---|---|---
Will Mainers ever get paid back for the Medicaid fraud Ali is alleged to have committed?
The gap between the money questioned and the money recovered remains substantial.
[Records we obtained under the Freedom of Access Act and published in April](https://substack.com/redirect/4426c7db-e54e-4171-85ee-97480ffd51ff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) documented $118,431.58 in repayments against roughly $1.6 million in alleged overpayments.
The foreclosure certificate adds a separate proceeding to that unfinished financial reckoning. How much the bank is seeking, what the state has claimed and whether either will recover its money will only be determined if or when the house is listed for sale.

More than a year after the Maine Wire originally exposed Gateway Community Service's for improperly billing Medicaid, Somali-American founder Abdullahi Ali has lost his home to foreclosure. Sep 8 | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Bangor Savings Bank has moved to foreclose on the Falmouth home of Abdullahi Ali, the Somali-American refugee poster child whose company collected roughly $5 million per year in MaineCare payments before the Maine Wire exposed allegations of systemic fraud and multiple failed audits the state had kept quiet. Ali's company, Gateway Community Services LLC, and its 501(c)(3) arm, Gateway Community Services Maine, were among the top recipients of Medicaid funding in the state of Maine from 2018 to 2025, according to MaineCare payment records obtained via a Freedom of Access Act request. In addition, Ali was awarded multiple lucrative no-bid contracts from the Mills administration -- and he received nearly $700,000 from the Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) during the COVID-19 pandemic. Yet with all that taxpayer money flowing into his bank account, Ali somehow forgot to pay his taxes in 2023 and 2024. Cumberland County tax lien and foreclosure records filed against the bougie million-dollar home Ali owned in the wealthy suburb of Portland show that the top Democrat activist owes $44,082.54 in back taxes and will no longer be able to sell his house. A clerk's certificate filed in Cumberland County Superior Court identifies Ali as the defendant and Maine Revenue Services as a party in interest in a case that concerns the Hardy Road property Ali put on the market for $1 million earlier this year, while he was reportedly spending much of his time in Kenya and Dubai. The Robinson Report can't expose fraudsters and scammers -- or the politicians who support them -- without subscribers. Support us today! The Cumberland County records appear to foreshadow a fight between Bangor Savings Bank and the state of Maine over who will get paid back first -- if at all. It's not clear how the Somali-American refugee was able to continue fraudulently billing Medicaid and receiving no-bid contracts from the Mills administration for several years while failing to pay his own income taxes. | | | | | | | ---|---|--- | May 21, 2025 | Gov. Janet Mills (D) poses with former Gateway Ass. Exec. Dir. State Rep. Deqa Dhalac, Gateway CEO Abdullahi Ali, and former Gateway employee turned Office of New American's policy analyst Elkhas Ahmed The foreclosure filing might be the only justice Maine taxpayers get, as no charges have been filed in relation to Gateway Community Services and Ali has refused to return from Africa since the Maine Wire exposed the fraudulent conduct of his business, a so-called "migrant services" agency at the center of the Maine Democratic Party's power structure. Indeed, rather than file charges in the Gateway case, Maine Attorney General Aaron Frey awarded the migrant agency $400,000 in opioid settlement money last year. For years, the company received millions of dollars annually through Maine's Medicaid program while Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) auditors continually found the company had overbilled the program. Even though three state audits found Gateway improperly billed MaineCare for more than $1.6 million in services, the state never stopped shoveling money into the agency until the Maine Wire published the audits and whistleblower allegations. As first reported in March of 2025, Gateway is intricately tied to the Maine Democratic Party: Rep. Deqa Dhalac (D-South Portland) served as an assistant executive director; Rep. Yusuf Yusuf (D-Portland) worked for the company before going on to found his own home health care agency; Ekhlas Ahmed, a former Gateway employee, now works as the "policy analyst" for the Office of New Americans, formed by Gov. Janet Mills but based on a bill from Dhalac; and Safiya Khalid, a Democratic activist in Lewiston, worked as an assistant to Ali before starting Gateway's political arm, the Community Organizing Alliance (COA). ? Now Ali faces a bank's attempt to foreclose on his home, with the state's tax collection agency also named in the proceeding. that Ali had listed the 3,312-square-foot property for $1 million shortly after Homeland Security Investigations agents appeared at Gateway's Lewiston office. That report cited Ali's public social media posts placing him largely in Kenya and Dubai following his unsuccessful 2024 campaign for president of Jubaland, a region of Somalia. Ali's overseas political ambitions helped bring his Maine business dealings under scrutiny. In March 2025, that Gateway Community Services LLC had received roughly $5 million per year in MaineCare payments from 2019 through 2025, according to records obtained under a Freedom of Access Act request. During that period, Ali also publicly described helping finance armed forces in Somalia, including purchases of weapons, ammunition and food. Ali bragged that the militia he was funding -- during a period when we now know he was not paying taxes on the more than $400,000 per year he earned from his government-funded gig -- would be used to topple the sitting president of Jubaland after the 2024 "election." The scrutiny intensified when former Gateway billing specialist came forward. In allegations , Bernardini said supervisors fabricated service hours and inflated Medicaid claims at Ali's direction. | | | | | | | ---|---|--- | May 14, 2025 | According to documents Bernardini provided to The Robinson Report, the former Gateway employee submitted a complaint to Maine State Auditor Matt Dunlap (D) in 2024 to report suspected fraud, but he never heard back from the Office of the State Auditor (OSA). Dunlap is now the Democratic nominee for Maine's Second Congressional District. Rather than moving swiftly to investigate and shut down Gateway, Maine Revenue Services sent Bernardini a letter informing him that it was auditing his taxes. Because he had moved to Florida during the Covid-19 shutdowns and Gateway had continued withholding taxes from his paycheck as if he were a Maine resident, the audit process determined that the state in fact owed Bernardini a substantial sum in overpaid taxes. Bernardini also believes that he was wrongfully terminated from Gateway for blowing the whistle; however, every employment law firm he's approached about suing Gateway for back pay has turned down his case. "I chose integrity over a cushy job," Bernardini said. Gateway has denied fraud. In response to our reporting, Ali called the Maine Wire "racist and hateful" in a post to X. "I make no apologies for building a successful business in Maine," he said. DHHS, meanwhile, identified substantial repayment obligations. Two earlier reviews resulted in demands for approximately $125,000 and $537,550 after adjustments. A subsequent audit covering March 2021 through December 2022 identified more than $1 million in additional questioned billings. On December 23, 2025, the Department of Health and Human Services suspended MaineCare payments to Gateway after determining there was a "credible allegation of fraud." DHHS upheld the suspension in May. Gateway then missed its July 17 deadline to appeal, . Now, Maine Revenue Services has identified $44,082.54 in unpaid state income taxes. Gateway has attributed the disputed billings to documentation deficiencies, changing guidance and administrative errors, as opposed to the intentional fraud alleged by Bernardini. | | ---|---|--- Secretary of State Shenna Bellows poses with Sen. Peter, President Obama and I founded the National Democratic Redistricting Committee as the first-ever strategic hub for the fair maps movement **because we needed to address a crisis that was getting out of hand.** Across the country, Republicans had gone out of their way to abuse the redistricting process and manipulate maps to steal power they didn’t earn. These guys didn’t invent gerrymandering. But it sure seemed like they were trying to perfect it. They engineered themselves an obscene 47-seat structural advantage in the U.S. House, which let them keep control even after losing the popular House vote in 2012. **President Obama and I believe that when the maps are fair, democracy works the way it’s supposed to. So we fought back.** The fair maps movement achieved incredible results in just a few short years. By the last midterm election in 2022, we were competing on what _The New York Times_ called “the fairest House map of the last 40 years.” **When Donald Trump instigated a national crisis of mid-decade redistricting, he did so as a direct and extreme response to the progress you and I have fought for. A kid from 53206 who built a career on bringing people together | | | | [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquchf2e3e-bIm5hAkq2zKIjvamPfag9y_bswSQjaYCFy9MjdWE1wV2uXo3NcOqsJcFtgsV_KgISdRGF7nV1t9x3Q6MPvYSIQo13QYrWCefxC-vRtq2qsjlX5BQPcE77_deoW5kY0_YWORIwigJ4JSEadqj9_1lkbbPgakFrVpbywalKR_PymFUPaEDCm5elUNhEJZY9rtN7fjB0Ky4MNF9m1dl0EZxZu4maBgLdHAk9I1-8IlktKjMeFT3Qj8FpL3IKupVPXYUajzKQXz4nM8zIr3opVzgzz4Z7NGr8LopyzGfk_h7htv2AjVM3ZFqCg6LcVUHVS4sFRMMn7F6lEJ5GgLCDkv_wwXDa_dYPybZfRoMw-_2UwnCqhNf-joS126uDYmBVYHIkf-CD6hGWHWxmxTNR8dpjPUgQbh6qizDsu5QzRV_vlgxYnlRSSP5l_Lc/4tv/YAI0zWqGRTGdFOqQQmbldg/h0/h001.QXh6iHWE_Bm1a4__5UB5yxaV3XvR01yKo5m6fcV9PP8) Derek, now that I'm Wisconsin's Democratic nominee for Governor, I wanted to take a minute to introduce myself properly. I grew up in Milwaukee's 53206 ZIP code, where my family faced food insecurity and the threat of eviction. **I know what it feels like when the system isn't built for people like me.** That's what got me into public service in the first place. I got my start in the Wisconsin Legislature, finding common ground with people I didn't always agree with to pass laws that actually helped people. Then I became Milwaukee County Executive, the youngest person and the first Black person to hold that office, where I brought together labor, business, and community organizations to build close to 1,000 units of affordable housing and push for universal childcare for working families. **I'm ready to take this same work ethic to the governor's office to make lives better for all Wisconsinites.** Wisconsin is one of the closest states in the country. Every one of our last three presidential elections was decided by less than a point. And my opponent? He's a far-right election denier who spent his time in Congress supporting Donald Trump and MAGA extremism. **That's the kind of race we're in, and we need a large coalition to defend this open seat.** **[_I'm ready for this fight, but I can't do it without support from people like you. clean_body: A kid from 53206 who built a career on bringing people together | | | | Derek, now that I'm Wisconsin's Democratic nominee for Governor, I wanted to take a minute to introduce myself properly. I grew up in Milwaukee's 53206 ZIP code, where my family faced food insecurity and the threat of eviction. I know what it feels like when the system isn't built for people like me. That's what got me into public service in the first place. I got my start in the Wisconsin Legislature, finding common ground with people I didn't always agree with to pass laws that actually helped people. Then I became Milwaukee County Executive, the youngest person and the first Black person to hold that office, where I brought together labor, business, and community organizations to build close to 1,000 units of affordable housing and push for universal childcare for working families. I'm ready to take this same work ethic to the governor's office to make lives better for all Wisconsinites. Wisconsin is one of the closest states in the country. Every one of our last three presidential elections was decided by less than a point. And my opponent? He's a far-right election denier who spent his time in Congress supporting Donald Trump and MAGA extremism. # Stand Up for Fairfax

Shelly Arnoldi, a veteran engineer, leads a grassroots effort in Fairfax County that puts families at the center of political action. By participating in community forums, round‐tables, and hands‐on workshops, you'll directly engage local leaders and shape policies affecting education and public services. This is a chance to counter government overreach, support liberty‐minded candidates, and build a network of civic‐focused citizens. Act now to ensure a future where our freedoms are protected.

|
### Community Advocacy
Shelly is running for CD-8 in efforts to Bring accountability and civic change to the entrenched 2 party system that has let our community down with wasteful spending and a greater commitment to identity politics than keeping our streets safe and our infrastructure sound.

Tonight, Tuesday, September 8, the Arlington County Civic Federation will host its Annual Candidates' Forum beginning at 7:00 p.m. This is an opportunity to hear from candidates for Virginia's 8th Congressional District and learn more about their views and priorities.

# [Mamdani taxed trophy homes. $100K rents jumped sevenfold.](https://substack.com/redirect/5d02673f-e87d-441a-a92d-27385787510a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Seven times as many Manhattan apartments **[now rent for more than $100,000](https://substack.com/redirect/a384fb0c-8d8b-4c2e-b87a-876b83370a09?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** a month, while **[Amazon warned a Mamdani-backed delivery bill](https://substack.com/redirect/4d19cd16-b43a-408d-b4e4-452aea6f1244?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** could add $664 a year for every city household.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5d02673f-e87d-441a-a92d-27385787510a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Median rent hits record:** Manhattan's median hit $5,295 in July, up 6%, Corcoran said. The top 10% averaged $17,464 after a 35% jump, and rentals above $50,000 more than doubled.
* **Second-home tax arrives:** The surcharge covers 1- to 3-family homes valued above $5 million and certain condos and co-ops assessed above $1 million. Mamdani said it will raise $500 million a year.
* **Homeowners fight City Hall:** 3 owners sued after notices went to about 17,000 properties. A lower court paused the rollout; an appeals court let the process resume while the fight continues.
* **Amazon warns $664 hit:** Intro 0518, backed by Mamdani and Council Member Tiffany Caban, could add $664 per household, lift per-package costs 267%, and put 40-plus partners and 5,000 workers at risk.

# [Nasdaq just forced $15.5B of buying into Musk's SpaceX](https://substack.com/redirect/5d02673f-e87d-441a-a92d-27385787510a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
JPMorgan says a Nasdaq-100 rebalance could force about **[$15.5 billion of passive buying](https://substack.com/redirect/4e3ee9d6-50e1-4edd-a123-69883d9d811d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** into SpaceX this month as its index weight jumps from 1.25% toward 2.25%.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5d02673f-e87d-441a-a92d-27385787510a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Float still thin:** SpaceX is already the 7th-largest Nasdaq-100 name near $2 trillion, yet its 1.25% weight ranks only 19th because of a small post-IPO public float.
* **Starlink cadence holds:** SpaceX **[completed its 80th Starlink launch](https://substack.com/redirect/969af1d3-8941-41e2-bf1d-50f7c12cf170?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** of 2026 on Sunday, ahead of a rocket switch-up that should help the company cut costs.
* **Orbital compute waits:** Musk is aiming for a late-2027 orbital data-center launch. Neuberger's Evelyn Chow called true scale a next-decade event, **[citing cooling, radiation and downlink hurdles.](https://substack.com/redirect/32612d7e-e2d5-4b2e-8f6b-6393d5b345c5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
* **Texas chip factory:** SpaceX and Tesla **[plan Terafab Texas in Grimes,](https://substack.com/redirect/80f0cb3b-676b-49e0-91bb-adddb2ede591?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** a more than 100 million-square-foot plant for Optimus, Cybercab and space-data-center chips. Initial phase is about $16.8 billion.

# [CoreWeave and Intel are now Nvidia's $99B problem](https://substack.com/redirect/5d02673f-e87d-441a-a92d-27385787510a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Nvidia **[disclosed about $99 billion of equity](https://substack.com/redirect/017b11c8-7db2-41ab-9719-d66807b35773?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** stakes as of July 26, plus $25 billion more in commitments, even as a key partner said AI compute demand may never be sated.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5d02673f-e87d-441a-a92d-27385787510a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Intel is the test:** The book includes a $30 billion Intel slice after Nvidia invested $5 billion alongside a pact to jointly develop data-center and PC products.
* **CoreWeave sits inside:** Several billion dollars of CoreWeave equity sit in the same portfolio. Short interest was 58,859,603 shares, or 16.92% of float, as of Aug. 14.
* **Iren sees no ceiling:** Iren co-CEO Daniel Roberts said it is really **[hard to see supply overtaking demand,](https://substack.com/redirect/efb71059-500a-4bfd-ab08-0c351a59d669?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/efb71059-500a-4bfd-ab08-0c351a59d669?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)as Iren prepares to spend up to $30 billion over the coming year.
* **Goldman maps the build:** Goldman Sachs expects U.S. data-center capacity to double from 2024 levels by the end of 2027 and more than triple by 2030, to about 125 GW.

# [Apple's $2,000 foldable is Ternus's opening act tomorrow](https://substack.com/redirect/5d02673f-e87d-441a-a92d-27385787510a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
New Apple CEO John Ternus **[hosts his first iPhone event Wednesday](https://substack.com/redirect/f3895df3-634e-4d88-9c2f-905e235f1918?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/f3895df3-634e-4d88-9c2f-905e235f1918?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)in Cupertino, with a foldable model widely expected after he succeeded Tim Cook on Sept. 1.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5d02673f-e87d-441a-a92d-27385787510a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Pro lineup expected:** The event is also widely expected to show iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max plus Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4.
* **Maps says America:** Apple Maps now shows Lake America[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/39b5819d-c60b-4607-ad92-f5d374771a3d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[for U.S. users](https://substack.com/redirect/39b5819d-c60b-4607-ad92-f5d374771a3d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after Trump's Aug. 27 order updated federal GNIS, matching Google. Canadian users still see Lake Ontario.
* **MapQuest keeps Ontario:** **[MapQuest kept calling it Lake Ontario](https://substack.com/redirect/e25fb58f-dbb9-4414-ad86-9e6a50c37b91?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and said usage hit about 50 times normal after hundreds of thousands of downloads, topping U.S. App Store navigation.
* **China chips tested:** Apple is[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/4a90d402-b59a-42e6-bd42-c6619208e74b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[testing CXMT memory chips](https://substack.com/redirect/4a90d402-b59a-42e6-bd42-c6619208e74b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** for iPhones and MacBooks sold in China and wants White House approval. Custom chips are barred, so a redesign may follow.

NextEra Energy closed a Department of Energy loan of **[up to $1.9 billion to restart Iowa's only nuclear plant,](https://substack.com/redirect/65868e0b-4c4b-43e2-b45b-0b3be8787b4c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as New York separately **[pursues 5 gigawatts of new reactors.](https://substack.com/redirect/63e59055-f1eb-4fb9-848a-e3e8a9a41c64?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5d02673f-e87d-441a-a92d-27385787510a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Duane Arnold target:** The 615-megawatt Linn County plant is slated to return by the first quarter of 2029, pending approvals, after NextEra announced the restart plan last October.
* **Financing office closed:** The deal ran through the Energy Department's Office of Energy Dominance Financing and is meant to add around-the-clock power to the regional grid, NextEra said Tuesday.
* **Hochul wants 5 GW:** Gov. Kathy Hochul is pursuing 5 gigawatts of new nuclear capacity, with at least 1 gigawatt at the New York Power Authority and a separate 4-gigawatt track.
* **Pause bill pending:** Sen. Kevin Parker's legislation would impose a 30-month pause on taxpayer and ratepayer support for new or restarted nuclear plants while a task force studies costs.

# [Von der Leyen eyes €10T of 'lazy' household deposits](https://substack.com/redirect/5d02673f-e87d-441a-a92d-27385787510a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen told French business leaders that **[€10 trillion in household cash savings is sitting idle](https://substack.com/redirect/8f69b055-c47f-4234-9a67-7b68f7f56620?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and should be put to work for European companies.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5d02673f-e87d-441a-a92d-27385787510a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Paris speech sets target:** She spoke Friday at MEDEF's La Rencontre des Entrepreneurs de France, arguing Europe has savings but those deposits remain on the sidelines of the real economy.
* **Debt clock is ticking:** Starting in 2028, repayment of the €800 billion NextGenerationEU Eurobond program comes due, raising the political premium on mobilizing private capital.
* **France still deep in red:** France is running new borrowing equal to 5.7% of GDP this year, with a parliamentary deadlock that rules out fiscal consolidation.
* **Digital euro next:** A digital-euro pilot is slated in 2 years, with foreign-account limits, digital ID and crypto rules described as the next tightening tools.

# [Meta's kids ruling: $567M. Zuck's next product: you.](https://substack.com/redirect/5d02673f-e87d-441a-a92d-27385787510a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Mark Zuckerberg argued[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/610455db-709d-43a1-a176-095696246057?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[personal superintelligence should be broadly distributed,](https://substack.com/redirect/610455db-709d-43a1-a176-095696246057?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/610455db-709d-43a1-a176-095696246057?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)even as a New Mexico judge ordered Meta to **[pay $567 million and overhaul teen protections](https://substack.com/redirect/3920a551-b621-47cc-864e-e26113d5e013?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** on Facebook and Instagram.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5d02673f-e87d-441a-a92d-27385787510a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Letter sets doctrine:** In a 14-page note titled "The Future is for Everyone," Zuckerberg said invention should be AI's purpose and a balance of power favoring individuals is the safety foundation.
* **Open models coming back:** Meta will resume releasing some open-source models, starting with Muse Glimmer, a 30-billion-parameter model that can run on a laptop or single consumer GPU.
* **Community fund attached:** A $1 billion Future is for Everyone Fund will back towns that host Meta data centers. In Richland Parish, Louisiana, teachers received a $50,000 bonus from tax revenue.
* **Judge orders teen overhaul:** Judge Bryan Biedscheid found a public nuisance and added $567 million on top of a March $375 million jury award, for nearly $942 million total. Meta said it will appeal.

# [Seoul eyes a $22.3B Texas plant. Its ministry won't confirm.](https://substack.com/redirect/5d02673f-e87d-441a-a92d-27385787510a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Korean media said Seoul and Washington agreed on about $22.3 billion for a 6.3-gigawatt gas plant in Encinal, Texas, but South Korea's Industry Ministry **[called the reports inaccurate.](https://substack.com/redirect/dd37766e-4ef7-4151-9412-94cc9d7f6e1c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5d02673f-e87d-441a-a92d-27385787510a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Edaily cites unnamed officials:** The outlet said the Encinal plant would be Seoul's first U.S. project under last year's trade deal and is meant to power rising AI data-center demand.
* **Trade-deal envelope is huge:** Under that pact, Seoul pledged $350 billion of U.S. investments in exchange for favorable tariffs on South Korean goods. Reports did not say Seoul would fund the whole Texas bill.
* **Other U.S. sites floated:** The same reports said Seoul is also weighing a large nuclear plant or an LNG project in Alaska. The ministry said no U.S. nuclear decision has been made.
* **Ministry: talks still open:** Officials said consultations continue and an announcement would come only after negotiations finish and parliamentary approval is considered.

body:
RITE files its third brief in key citizenship verification case |
---
| |
---
| | **RITE Defends Arizona’s Proof of Citizenship Laws at the Supreme Court**
**WASHINGTON, D.C.** — Restoring Integrity and Trust in Elections (RITE), joined by the Center for Election Confidence and the Honest Elections Project, has [filed an amicus brief](https://us.list-manage.com/1CKMmo6Zk0Z?e=ea91f782ea&c2id=bf38de461872f35bd013169f413b699e) with the U.S. Supreme Court in _Republican National Committee v. Mi Familia Vota_ , urging the Court to reverse a Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals decision restricting Arizona’s ability to enforce citizenship requirements in its elections. You can also read Fox News' coverage of our joint brief [here](https://us.list-manage.com/rAD47f9riZW?e=ea91f782ea&c2id=bf38de461872f35bd013169f413b699e).

The brief marks RITE’s third amicus filing in the case. RITE’s brief explains how the Ninth Circuit misread the National Voter Registration Act (NVRA) in striking down provisions requiring documentary proof of citizenship from applicants using Arizona’s state voter-registration form and that election officials remove noncitizens from the voter rolls regardless of the proximity to the election.

“The Constitution gives states the responsibility to determine who is qualified to vote, and that responsibility includes the ability to enforce those qualifications,” said RITE President Justin Riemer. “Further, states shouldn’t be forced to ignore ineligible registrants on their voter rolls, especially near an election. Election officials must be able to correct errors and ensure that those participating in American elections are legally qualified to do so.”

RITE’s brief asks the Supreme Court to reverse the Ninth Circuit and hold that the NVRA does not prevent Arizona from requiring proof of citizenship on its state voter-registration form or from removing people who were never legally eligible to register within 90 days of a federal election. ###

| | | Oregon didn't just adopt vote-by-mail. We INVENTED it. **So when the US Supreme Court cleared the way for Trump's executive order restricting mail-in ballots, understand what that means: ** No state has more on the line than Oregon. This order isn't aimed at some abstract "voting system." **It targets how every single Oregonian votes.** Here's what Trump’s USPS order does. It orders the Postal Service to deliver ballots only to voters on a federal list — a list built by THIS administration. Their postmaster already said the quiet part out loud: states that don't hand over their voter data likely won't have mail ballots delivered at all. Now here's what I know. **I'm Oregon's chief elections officer. We have taken this administration to court twice — over their demand for your voter data, and over their first election order. We won both times.** **And now we’ve filed suit again. ** **The Constitution hasn't changed** since then. States run elections. Not presidents. Not postmasters. And this November, Oregon will run the same safe, fair, accurate vote-by-mail election we've run for 25 years — and I will use every power of this office to make sure of it. **[But fighting them in court is only one way to defend our elections. We must have the resources to communicate about what’s at stake — every lawsuit, every rule change, every attempt to rewrite how Oregon votes. That’s why I’m using my campaign to help travel around the state and talk directly to voters too. clean_body: | | | = | | | Oregon didn't just adopt vote-by-mail. We INVENTED it. So when the US Supreme Court cleared the way for Trump's executive order restricting mail-in ballots, understand what that means: No state has more on the line than Oregon. This order isn't aimed at some abstract "voting system." It targets how every single Oregonian votes. Here's what Trump’s USPS order does. It orders the Postal Service to deliver ballots only to voters on a federal list — a list built by THIS administration. Their postmaster already said the quiet part out loud: states that don't hand over their voter data likely won't have mail ballots delivered at all. Now here's what I know. I'm Oregon's chief elections officer. We have taken this administration to court twice — over their demand for your voter data, and over their first election order. We won both times. And now we’ve filed suit again. The Constitution hasn't changed since then. States run elections. Not presidents. Not postmasters. And this November, Oregon will run the same safe, fair, accurate vote-by-mail election we've run for 25 years — and I will use every power of this office to make sure of it. = = They think they can push around a small state like Oregon. name: Darline Graham
subject: A promise made a long time ago
body:
Some moments you never forget. This was one of them. |
---

Fellow Patriot,

There's a moment I've never forgotten.

I was 11 when we lost our mom. A little over a year later, we lost our dad, too. Our family business - a pool hall and bar right on Main Street in Central, South Carolina - still needed to be run. And I was wondering what came next.

[](http://links.freedomfirstalert.com/u/click?_t=9ca143e971904d26a973d002cb0ae7f7&_m=b6aecdc320a4440384b489a59591c409&_e=dsenfqVnxGiNkZnpv7qrNrUAhn4Fbw8CFMyZG3ALZ2pCsrO-QFFojS40yQPaADc67TqhKvcTEOJZuwZRTAJYBUSVK5YKQgy83a4_yF5H4NQH5yZrwCDI48veNnih0BjybHnDmn9xgHIhHe9aj3IoRoH7j7IbSTKOLRNlj-R2wIMX20iVBI5rfdOvswh4-VmWIlPh8UvV_5Pst3pF9X1jjnB4907kZaN5yH8FWh4kYF0XZ1lS8jYN_H9k1gYSgftqHvScTlAJt0t3FbIETfR5ucoWurVmfcmqvaFdmdObqYC5mQL47eTlAurJgJSoF7LrcZOl-uGu_Oi-pv97xMbluOrbO33CAkby2daUL_DV_XCAp6qoCZaaZ7hIlWERIKzwaLVRZJSaL5ySQZQp2coVIMuzY-sywvBqYT5RAK512NIh3NVmVnRj20gG4vTU6kYAak82B8w-NZtrcI4oGHrHP4MuW_ue2MitPlwLt8IMWgthCF3CDddQLSYdzLXYQml4tWJpSYoDYH57o2PCYE2cpESS2cZOV-IjP0mIz4Udn1wyS65wQhqt1x25a8jpi-T2TCirkcIF5gSF44x-8MMX_vt58WQQ1l7PkD6A_SmrCiVxFGs64Sn-cIm1apwhWYercgfggZS1CrGu-1mD83Mn5MezrsCkAVp9QVxGuZeNjTFDC844Y05IThfY9OKmGgGRSrOCaQPy-FXgjDsKA75QCL3c3xkm7BsqeFM6rdomyG0%3D)
My brother Lindsey figured it out.

He was in college, and he came home on weekends to take care of me and keep the doors open. It wasn't easy for him, but he made sure I had what I needed. That's just what he always did.

Our folks never finished high school. They ran the Sanitary Cafe - part bar, part restaurant, part pool hall - and we lived in the back of it, right there on Main Street. Lindsey swept those floors right alongside me. We both heard those conversations of working people from the textile mills, stopping in after their shift, talking about what they needed, what they hoped for, and what kept them up at night.

Those people shaped him a lot more than much else ever did.

After college and law school, he joined the Air Force. There he served as a military prosecutor and defense attorney. Even after South Carolina sent him to the Statehouse, Congress and finally, the Senate, he kept his commission. His service included short deployments to Afghanistan and Iraq where he stood shoulder to shoulder with 19-year-olds from little towns just like ours who were willing to give everything.

You want to know why he fought so hard in Washington? _Because he knew who was counting on him._

It's the family in Greenville stretching a paycheck that doesn't quite reach. The veteran in Spartanburg that earned every benefit he gets. The business owner in Florence who built something from nothing and doesn't need the government to make it harder.

These are his people. And right now, they need someone in their corner.

**The radical left in this country today:** they want open borders, higher taxes, and more government in your life. They'll smile and tell you it's for your own good.

I'm here to tell you it isn't.

**[Fellow Patriot, I'm asking for your help today.](http://links.freedomfirstalert.com/u/click?_t=9ca143e971904d26a973d002cb0ae7f7&_m=b6aecdc320a4440384b489a59591c409&_e=dsenfqVnxGiNkZnpv7qrNrUAhn4Fbw8CFMyZG3ALZ2pCsrO-QFFojS40yQPaADc67TqhKvcTEOJZuwZRTAJYBUSVK5YKQgy83a4_yF5H4NQH5yZrwCDI48veNnih0BjybHnDmn9xgHIhHe9aj3IoRoH7j7IbSTKOLRNlj-R2wIMX20iVBI5rfdOvswh4-VmWIlPh8UvV_5Pst3pF9X1jjnB4907kZaN5yH8FWh4kYF0XZ1lS8jYN_H9k1gYSgftqVNCszuAV7_AyqWhS7I1jv9uFPLc3I8CzeHzspg255IcSoaauO47nKHvkT4EXX7jWNj50WpYZ9-cWrJuxfbVsi2lsKVz3JwxP6CdP6wv0T0qUlVysKzawyfPmqDHx7k9R5Ug5Gz5UzE5OuQkd8ZCkV8Tknq783Xm_KBFW-50XY1SQORnJVsU2bGPqgrJjcegaAAgWtz0UYa4NqYS6VPJpLovOAzT-nkafv8uLnOnBSNYAfQC6JZab9KSIcBop7d7tUuXqpKxeL_FYMnuiHMl9wdaHiQP4PdqHbXiaKSBcZEZXItq9Zntf8aHindMiugYfYwHULZdZ68BtZrY8wNLrj1QjW24qjic0cbemjJOhSwRJJoEEuPeXBLPBjZ4Krft4FWNA4wBi6I4b0ECyatVlpU3UPfmvgRIKzLhgGZlzK4TLQtUDOsYpw2-Tzmr1zk_OjfhiOTrFcvtxQ65XBYP1kAIrv4PosvFkzKHQ7xTji9Q%3D)** The legacy my brother built can never be replicated, but I can honor him by working as hard as he did every single day for the great people of South Carolina.

All those years ago, he promised me things would be okay. Now, it's my turn to pick up where he left off and make sure the people he loved, South Carolinians from the Grand Strand to the Golden Corner, are okay.

clean_body: Some moments you never forget. This was one of them. | Fellow Patriot, There's a moment I've never forgotten. I was 11 when we lost our mom. A little over a year later, we lost our dad, too. Our family business - a pool hall and bar right on Main Street in Central, South Carolina - still needed to be run. And I was wondering what came next. My brother Lindsey figured it out. He was in college, and he came home on weekends to take care of me and keep the doors open. It wasn't easy for him, but he made sure I had what I needed. That's just what he always did. Our folks never finished high school. They ran the Sanitary Cafe - part bar, part restaurant, part pool hall - and we lived in the back of it, right there on Main Street. Lindsey swept those floors right alongside me. We both heard those conversations of working people from the textile mills, stopping in after their shift, talking about what they needed, what they hoped for, and what kept them up at night. Those people shaped him a lot more than much else ever did. After college and law school, he joined the Air Force. There he served as a military prosecutor and defense attorney. Even after South Carolina sent him to the Statehouse, Congress and finally, the Senate, he kept his commission. His service included short deployments to Afghanistan and Iraq where he stood shoulder to shoulder with 19-year-olds from little towns just like ours who were willing to give everything. You want to know why he fought so hard in Washington? Because he knew who was counting on him. It's the family in Greenville stretching a paycheck that doesn't quite reach. The veteran in Spartanburg that earned every benefit he gets. The business owner in Florence who built something from nothing and doesn't need the government to make it harder. These are his people. And right now, they need someone in their corner. The radical left in this country today: they want open borders, higher taxes, and more government in your life. They'll smile and tell you it's for your own good. I'm here to tell you it isn't. The legacy my brother built can never be replicated, but I can honor him by working as hard as he did every single day for the great people of South Carolina. I am starting this General Election behind financially. All those years ago, he promised me things would be okay. Now, it's my turn to pick up where he left off and make sure the people he loved, South Carolinians from the Grand Strand to the Golden Corner, are okay. I can't let him down. That's why, when President Trump asked me to run, I answered the call. Thank you, from the bottom of my heart. Darline Graham | | Paid for by Darline Graham Majority Fund, a joint fundraising committee authorized by and composed of Darline for Senate, Fund for America's Future, Security is Strength PAC, and NRSC. 228 S. # Join Us for Our Autism Support Group Today
---
|
---
| We invite you to join us for our **Autism Support Group** **Today, September 8th at 4:00 PM PST / 7:00 PM EST** via Zoom. Whether you are a parent, caregiver, family member, self advocate, or professional, this monthly gathering provides a welcoming and supportive space to connect with others who understand the autism journey. Our support group is an opportunity to share experiences, ask questions, exchange resources, celebrate victories, and receive encouragement from a compassionate community. Together, we learn from one another, discuss challenges and solutions, and build meaningful relationships that remind us we are never alone. At Autism Health, we believe that connection is one of the most powerful tools for healing and hope. No matter where you are on your journey, you are welcome to join us. **Advance registration through Zoom is required to attend.** Please register using the link below to receive your Zoom access information. We look forward to seeing you **later today, September 8th at 4:00 PM PST!**

| The countdown has begun for the **2027 Autism Health Summit** , taking place **April 29 through May 1, 2027** , at **The Legacy Center Resort & Spa** in **San Diego, California**. name: Troy Downing
subject: Will you pray for a veteran?
body:
I am humbly asking you to lend me your thoughts and prayers today.

| [](https://trk.emails.troydowning._cmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTM1JmV4X3RpZD0yMDI2MDkwOF9XUy1UOS4xMTAxMTdfdDIwMTU2ODUtMjg5OSZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249MjAyNjA5MDhfV1MtVDkuMTEwMTE3X3QyMDE1Njg1LTI4OTkifQ/Fn_nUlNHb06Ed9Wxcffn7w)
---
Peter,
Do you believe in the power of prayer?
My name’s Troy Downing. When America faced its darkest hour after 9/11, I knew I couldn't just sit on the sidelines. I enlisted in the U.S. Air Force and served eight years in a Combat Search and Rescue squadron, deploying twice to Afghanistan.
On those missions, flying into danger to rescue wounded soldiers, you rely on something much bigger than yourself. Through every deployment and dark night, God’s guiding hand was our shield and protection.
Now, as a Member of Congress working to defend the American Dream and protect our GOP Majority, the battlefield has changed, but the spiritual stakes are just as high. I still rely on God’s unchanging, guiding hand every single day.
[If you believe in God and the power of prayer to guide our leaders and protect our land, I am humbly asking you to lend me your thoughts and prayers today.](https://trk.emails.troydowning._cmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTM1JmV4X3RpZD0yMDI2MDkwOF9XUy1UOS4xMTAxMTdfdDIwMTU2ODUtMjg5OSZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249MjAyNjA5MDhfV1MtVDkuMTEwMTE3X3QyMDE1Njg1LTI4OTkifQ/ZZGKoHEcQsln7xAGbTgzWA)

| [SEND A PRAYER TO VETERAN DOWNING](https://trk.emails.troydowning._cmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmYW1vdW50PTM1JmV4X3RpZD0yMDI2MDkwOF9XUy1UOS4xMTAxMTdfdDIwMTU2ODUtMjg5OSZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249MjAyNjA5MDhfV1MtVDkuMTEwMTE3X3QyMDE1Njg1LTI4OTkifQ/-kPa9tQ_vvDQ5aEPCmYgAg)
---
Your faith and your prayers are the greatest support I could ever ask for as we fight to keep our nation strong and free.
God Bless,
Troy Downing
U.S. Representative, Montana's 2nd District

clean_body: You don't make it harder to vote unless you're afraid of losing. | = Peter, We're calling this what it is: voter suppression — plain and simple. = Texas' secretary of state has assigned more than 1.2 million voters a "suspended" voter registration status — including lifelong Texas residents and people who vote regularly. These voters weren't given advance notice. Many may not even know their registration has been suspended until they arrive at the polls this November. And that's the point. Republicans want to make it harder for Texans to vote them out of power. It's time for us to fight back. = | = Texas Republicans are trying to rig the system because they can see Democratic momentum building. They know what we know: Texas can flip. It can flip because of EMILYs List women like the four candidates running to flip Texas Supreme Court seats; or women like Katy Padilla Stout (TX-23) , who is running to turn an open U.S. House seat; Lizzie Fletcher (TX-07) and Sylvia Garcia (TX-29) , who are fighting to hold critical Democratic seats in the battle for the House majority; and Gina Hinojosa (TX-GOV) , who has built a statewide coalition ready to elect Texas' first Democratic pro-choice woman governor in decades. These women are taking on a Republican machine that will do whatever it can to hold onto power. It's hard to believe this Friday will be 25 years since 9/11. Like [93% of Americans](https://substack.com/redirect/e3930af3-70cf-4e72-af14-646f1aa51063?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) who were at least 10 years old that day, I remember exactly where I was when I heard the news. I was a 27-year-old Army officer teaching military and constitutional law at West Point. During my 8 a.m. class in Thayer Hall, word came that a plane had struck the North Tower of the World Trade Center. Like so many Americans that morning, we didn't immediately understand what we were watching. By the time class ended, we all did.
Walking back to my office, I passed a cadet at a pay phone leaving a voicemail for his father.
"Dad? I heard the Pentagon got hit. Call me and let me know you're okay. I love you."
I can still hear it vividly.
Later that morning, I sat in the cafeteria at West Point with soldiers and cadets glued to CNN and Fox News as the towers came down. Fresh out of Airborne and Air Assault training, I knew I'd be getting nto the fight. I also knew that some of my students, the young men and women sitting in that room, would soon be fighting in Afghanistan. Like everyone else, I was trying to understand what had just happened. But I also felt the patriotic instinct that had been drilled into me as a soldier: _What can I do now?_
West Point immediately moved to Force Protection Condition Delta, the military's highest level of security, and the academy suddenly looked and felt different. Soldiers with M-16s were posted around West Point, and every car coming onto the grounds was searched. When we heard that volunteers might be needed to help with the search at the World Trade Center, I immediately put my name forward. I asked for permission to take my motorcycle down to New York to help, but the request was denied. So I started pulling nightly guard duty. The whole place felt different. We had spent our careers preparing for the possibility of war somewhere else and now New York was burning less than 50 miles away. I remember how frustrating that was. I was a soldier, the country had just been attacked, and all I wanted was some way to be useful - to get in the fight I was trained for.
So I did the next best thing I could think of. I borrowed a book about al-Qaeda from a colleague who specialized in terrorism and stayed up most of the night reading it. The next morning, I threw out the lecture I had planned and taught my cadets about Osama bin Laden, al-Qaeda, political Islam and the Taliban. Those cadets in my class hung on every word - they knew we'd all be going soon and we needed to get smart quick.
After class, I walked into Colonel Patrick Finnegan's office and told my boss I wanted out of my two-year teaching assignment so I could join the fight with the 82nd Airborne or the 101st Airborne, where I was supposed to be assigned next.
He reminded me that I had made a promise to teach and needed to honor it - but he expected and appreciated my desire to get into the fight - and that I'd be called to go soon enough, but the Army needed people in places other than the front lines for right now. If I called the Pentagon like I requested, he warned me, they would call him, and he would tell them he needed me there for right now. I knew he was right, even if it was not what I wanted to hear. So I gritted my teeth and stayed.
Looking back now, that conversation in Colonel Finnegan's office marked the beginning of a road that would eventually take me to Iraq as a paratrooper in the 82nd Airborne and years later to Congress and the Pentagon.
# **The Loss of Michele**
But the events of September 11 were more than changing the course of my professional life. They were becoming painfully personal. My best friend since age 6, Chris Norbeck, had recently begun dating a 27-year-old woman named Michele Hoffmann, and I had watched the relationship take shape four months earlier on a trip to Cancun, when it was still new and full of possibility. It was the first time I saw him completely head over heels in love.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9c851b7e-ac35-4ed2-9951-415c9212dc91?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Michele, Chris, and Me.
Michele worked at Cantor Fitzgerald on the upper floors of the North Tower. Her father, Frederick, worked there too. Both were killed that morning along with 656 of their coworkers. This represented the largest loss of life suffered by any single organization in the attacks and nearly a quarter of all those killed in New York City. A total of 18 people from Bucks County also perished, including Josh Reiss, who was five months into his term at Cantor Fitzgerald.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a014f9fe-c106-4575-b2f1-fab40fca42fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
J _osh Reiss, former newspaper paperboy for the Bucks County Courier. Graduate of the University of South Carolina._
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/18d72fe6-b706-40d3-89a7-1eb19baf2300?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Howard Lutnick, now the U.S. Commerce Secretary, was Cantor Fitzgerald's CEO at the time. He avoided death that day because he was taking his five-year-old son Kyle to his first day of kindergarten. His younger brother Gary was killed that day. Within weeks, Cantor made a $45 million payment to the victims' families. The firm later pledged 25% of its profits for five years and provided the families with 10 years of health coverage, ultimately delivering $180 million in support. He eventually built the firm back even bigger, with 60 employees being the children of those who perished that day.
##### **65% Were 'Extremely Proud to be An American'\- Today it's 33%**
I remember how different the country felt in the days after September 11. People were scared and angry, but there was also a real sense that we were in this together. American flags seemed to show up everywhere. You saw them outside homes, over roads, on fire trucks, in store windows. Lee Greenwood's "God Bless the U.S.A.," which had been released nearly two decades earlier, was suddenly everywhere again and climbed to [No. 16 on the ](https://substack.com/redirect/c8ae4ff3-8ff8-461f-8b37-8b32b2863fce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[Billboard](https://substack.com/redirect/c8ae4ff3-8ff8-461f-8b37-8b32b2863fce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[ Hot 100](https://substack.com/redirect/c8ae4ff3-8ff8-461f-8b37-8b32b2863fce?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). To this day, it gets me choked to think about how unified we were - and when I hear that song - it still fires up when it's Toby Keith's "Courtesy of the Red, White and Blue."
[Gallup](https://substack.com/redirect/7900075d-80c1-43f9-9675-7790f45a0f2c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) found that the share of Americans who described themselves as "extremely proud" to be American surged to between 65 and 70% in the years immediately following 9/11. Today, that number is 33%, the lowest Gallup has recorded since it began asking the question in 2001.
Some of what followed September 11 brought out the very best in the country. People wanted to serve, and they found whatever way they could to do it. Americans lined up around blood centers to donate. Thousands of volunteers made their way to New York, Washington DC and Shanksville, PA (the crash site of Flight 93), while others joined the Red Cross, enlisted in the military, started charities or simply found ways to help the people around them. Communities gathered for candlelight vigils and filled parks, churches and town squares to mourn together. American flags seemed to appear everywhere. I remember all of that because the attacks seemed to crack open something in the country. It was an extraordinary thing to witness, and 25 years later, I wish we had more of it.
Some of what followed deserves a more complicated reckoning. Muslim and Arab Americans along with Sikhs and others perceived to be Muslim or Middle Eastern were suddenly treated with suspicion, and [hate crimes rose sharply](https://substack.com/redirect/3e3e5c10-30c6-477f-ab1a-bf69e18b05c2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the days after the attacks. President George W. Bush deserves credit for recognizing that danger early. Six days after 9/11, he visited the Islamic Center of Washington and famously said, "[Islam is peace](https://substack.com/redirect/8892f77c-ff96-4271-9832-2d9979413549?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg),"making clear that the United States was fighting terrorists, not Muslims. I mentioned his leadership [last 9/11](https://substack.com/redirect/2376f5aa-d7f6-49f8-b5a0-eeb8603db02c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at the Bush Presidential Library when they asked me to give my reflections on his response leadership, even though we are of different political parties. It's the type of unity I try to live my life by, and instill in my two teenage kids Maggie and Jack.
But fear was growing in the country. Over time, it became part of the argument for going to war in Iraq, even though Iraq had not attacked us on September 11th or were connected to it. By 2003, [69% of Americans believed Saddam Hussein had been personally involved in 9/11](https://substack.com/redirect/1eb63cda-0218-49d9-8938-56921ae7d98d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). He wasn't. Those of us who spoke up were often ostracized - I've lost Army buddies and friends for speaking up after I left active duty, even though it wasn't politically popular and I was still a registered Independent.
Fear and anger sometimes make us reckless, overriding rational judgment. Some of our fellow Americans were treated shamefully. But 25 years later, I still believe we can recover some of what was best about that moment without repeating what was worst about what came afterward.
This Friday, I will be thinking first about the nearly 3,000 people who were killed 25 years ago. The men and women who went to work that morning and never came home. The 125 people killed at the Pentagon who are often forgotten. The passengers and crew of Flight 93 who learned what was happening and courageously fought back against the hijackers, bringing the plane down near Shanksville, Pennsylvania, before it could reach what was most likely the U.S. Capitol.
I will also think about what ordinary Americans did for one another that day. In less than eight hours, roughly [500,000 people were evacuated by water](https://substack.com/redirect/6d4c70da-93ac-499e-9a5c-c8f9b5a4f432?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the largest maritime evacuation in recorded history - even larger than Dunkirk. People in private boats came to the rescue of New Yorkers stranded in Lower Manhattan.
But the list of people harmed by September 11 did not stop growing when the fires went out. Hundreds of thousands of responders, workers, residents and students were exposed to the toxic dust that settled over Lower Manhattan. Many became sick years later with respiratory illnesses and cancers. Today, the federal World Trade Center Health Program cares for more than [150,000 responders and survivors](https://substack.com/redirect/4fe0b9e1-c2ad-49c7-ac8c-e2947924959f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) across the country. More than 9,000 people have died from these illnesses - 3x the number of deaths on 9/11. More than 1000 victims have never been identified in the recovery efforts, stunting for many the closure of a burial.
So when we say "never forget," I hope we mean all of them. Twenty-five years later, remembering September 11 also means keeping our promise to take care of the survivors who are still living with its consequences and our military veterans who answered our nation's call. But it's also a call to rekindle the unity our fellow Americans had - where our political, economic and cultural differences didn't matter - because we were all Americans that day. Let us know what are you doing to hopefully bring back that unity?
Thank you for reading today's column. Your readership and support mean a great deal to me. #Neverforget.

Let us know what are you doing to hopefully bring back that unity? Thank you for reading today's column. Your readership and support mean a great deal to me. #Neverforget. body:
I wanted to follow up with you about this exciting event we're doing with OBKLA to say thank you.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/X3r9w4qnTcn?e=3cf484ad56&c2id=56d6f92d273ed6c9240a33982acf5cba)
| | Hi Peter,
I hope you had a nice Labor Day Weekend! I wanted to follow-up as we have a few slots left for our thank you event on Monday. We’ll be toasting to a successful campaign, thanking our volunteers, and making meals for the community.
Kids also welcome.
[RSVP here](https://us.list-manage.com/P0PNGDkCaeI?e=3cf484ad56&c2id=56d6f92d273ed6c9240a33982acf5cba) and hope to see you on Monday!
Nick
---
| | | | |
---
| | Peter,
I wanted to give you the summer off from my emails after you carried me to such a strong victory in early June!
But school is back in session — with my new screen time policy officially in effect — and I got back last week from another very successful session of Camp Harmony (our biggest yet!). And on September 9th, LAUSD’s new camp, which I’ve been working to spearhead, will officially open its doors. It’s hard to believe summer is already over, but there are lots of exciting things to come back to.
I wanted to reach out and invite you to a post-election thank you and service event with **Our Big Kitchen Los Angeles (OBKLA) on Monday, September 14th at 6 PM.**
Sign up here: [https://volunteer.obkla.org/acts/console.php?console_id=0375&console_type=event_list&res_code=pwoBDv&ht=1](https://us.list-manage.com/EyCWc2cla4K?e=3cf484ad56&c2id=56d6f92d273ed6c9240a33982acf5cba)
There’s no contribution required; just come join us to make sandwiches, have some refreshments, give back, and spend some time together.
OBKLA is an entirely volunteer-run kitchen that prepares and distributes meals to people in need throughout Los Angeles. I’m excited to partner with them for an evening of service in the Mid-Wilshire area — and to have a chance to thank so many of you who helped make our June victory possible.
Thank you again for your continued support. I hope to see you on the 14th!
---

Team Mackenzie,I hope you had a wonderful and safe Labor Day weekend.It was an incredible weekend on the ground across the Greater Lehigh Valley. We had a **great reception at the 91st Annual Pen Argyl Labor Day Parade** , where we had the opportunity to meet voters, talk about the issues that matter to our communities, and share our message of **Delivering for Our Community**.And our volunteers were everywhere.Thank you to every volunteer who spent the weekend knocking doors, talking with voters, and taking our message directly to neighborhoods across the Greater Lehigh Valley.**This weekend, we broke a campaign record for the most doors knocked in a single day.** That doesn’t happen without an incredible team willing to put in the work.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/ZMNHLgp9HYo?e=5ccada9200&c2id=772b190546f65300d48df506f9534e27)
| | (Click on Video Above)**And that work matters, especially when our opponent refuses to face the voters.****Today was supposed to be debate day.** WFMZ had reserved today to give the voters of Pennsylvania’s 7th Congressional District the opportunity to hear directly from both candidates, compare our records, and make an informed decision.Instead, **Bob Brooks is hiding.** Brooks is refusing to debate until late October, after many Pennsylvania voters will have already cast their mail-in ballots.**That isn’t fair to the voters.** What is Bob Brooks afraid to answer for?Stealing more than $160,000 from his own family? Screwing over his own employees and breaking state law? Calling our volunteer firefighters “shitbags”? Or is he worried about what else may come out?Now WFMZ is proposing debates in late September, giving voters who plan to vote by mail the opportunity to hear from both candidates **before they cast their ballots.** There is no excuse to keep hiding.**Bob, it’s time to stop running from the voters.** The voters deserve answers.
The voters deserve a debate.
And I’m ready to show up.I’m ready to talk about my record, talk about what I’ve delivered for the Greater Lehigh Valley, and debate the issues that matter to our communities.

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138808127/645268688/789508428?refcode=260908_RG_RFK-measles&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTcxOSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmY2YzOWRlZS1iN2FiLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=K4FIVqe5lSA_X3s6kkzmcKGkwOT9SE2tfs5mT7xuXCw=)
CDC staff had already accepted Pennsylvania’s determination that the deaths were linked to measles. Then Kennedy intervened—and the public tally changed.
That is gross political interference with public-health data, plain and simple.
**[Will you donate $10 today to help us win a Democratic House majority and hold Robert F Kennedy Jr. accountable?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138808128/645268689/789508428?refcode=260908_RG_RFK-measles&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTcxOSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmY2YzOWRlZS1iN2FiLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=K4FIVqe5lSA_X3s6kkzmcKGkwOT9SE2tfs5mT7xuXCw=)**
The American people depend on the CDC for facts that can protect their families. Those facts cannot be rewritten whenever they become inconvenient for a political appointee.
As the top Democrat on the Oversight Committee, I want the emails, the directives, and testimony under oath. Why did Kennedy intervene? What evidence did he rely on? Who carried out the order? And has HHS pressured scientists to change any other public-health data?
**We cannot let this become normal. A health secretary who manipulates a federal disease tally is not protecting the public — he is protecting himself.**
House Republicans will not conduct the aggressive investigation this demands. But if we take back the House, we can compel answers and expose every step of this decision.

#### **1\. Gloria Steinem Died One Signature Short of the ERA |**_**Cliff Schecter * September 5**_
She died at ninety-two and every outlet in America ran the same obituary. Here is what none of them ran: the Equal Rights Amendment has been ratified by thirty-eight states and is still not in the Constitution, and the reasons are a deadline Congress wrote in 1979 and an opinion Trump's Justice Department issued in 2020. Both are fixable. This piece is the how.
## [Gloria Steinem Died One Signature Short of the ERA](https://substack.com/redirect/b1efea10-95c6-4d91-85eb-0865b1895a28?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

#### **2\. Russia Has 1,000 Ships With No Country |**_**Lawrence Winnerman * September 6**_
There is a fleet of roughly a thousand aging tankers sailing under flags of convenience, owned through shells nobody can trace, and it is dragging anchors across the undersea cables that carry Europe's internet and electricity. Nobody can legally stop them. Worse, nobody seems willing to try. Thirty-five hundred words on the most consequential thing happening at sea, and I have not seen it explained anywhere else this clearly.

#### **3\. Epstein Emailed "trump tower" on Nov. 13, 2016 | **_**Ellie Leonard * August 17**_
Five days after the election, Jeffrey Epstein told a contact exactly where he was. Ellie found it in the files. Nobody else did. This is what an actual investigative reporter does with a document dump while cable news is running a panel about it.
## [Epstein Emailed "trump tower" on Nov. 13, 2016](https://substack.com/redirect/c0632fe5-8426-48b7-aad4-6978d452ca11?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

#### **4\. Hunter Biden on His Father 's Health, Recovery, and the Media | **_**Cliff Schecter and David Shuster * August 19**_
Ninety minutes, no handlers, no ground rules. He draws a distinction about addiction I have never heard anybody make out loud -- not cured, not still an addict, in recovery and permanently vulnerable -- and then explains exactly what that means he can never do again. He walks through the money: his paintings, about two hundred thousand a year, every single buyer hauled before Congress to testify under oath, set against billions in federal contracts going to the current president's family. He says what he actually thinks about Kamala Harris, which he could have skated past and didn't. He did not dodge one question. Not one.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/64e61b40-5f9a-4c3e-8d6c-aafeb99b8942?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
#### **5\. Andy Borowitz Has Stopped Pretending to Be Neutral |**_**Cliff Schecter August 16**_
"I am a Democrat. I've never pretended to be both sidesy." Ninety minutes with the man who created Fresh Prince of Bel-Air on the life of a comedy writer, what Fox News actually wanted when they booked him, and why equal-opportunity satire is a lie when one side is doing all the lying.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/9b40b1a8-5ba2-44ec-bbf2-0c6fbe2cdd7a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
#### **6\. Raskin: Trump Pardoned Him. He Molested a Child. Then He Tried to Buy Silence. |**_**Cliff Schecter * September 3**_
Congressman Jamie Raskin walks us through _Pardons, Inc._ , his committee's report on how executive clemency became a cash business -- who paid, who got out, and what it cost the people they hurt. The case in that headline is one of them. Raskin has spent a career explaining constitutional machinery to people who would rather not hear it, and he is very good at it, and he is doing it here while fighting cancer. If you want to understand what has actually been sold off in the last two years, start with this hour.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/e3e66839-3e4a-429d-966f-6405dd79ae87?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
That is three weeks. Not a year, not a greatest-hits reel. Three weeks.
That is the whole pitch, and it is the only one I have: this is what it looks like when the people reading the thing are the ones paying for it. No network. No billionaire. No sponsor who gets nervous.
If you are already a paid subscriber, you have read all six and you are the reason they exist. Thank you! Nothing below is for you. Go flip the burgers.
For everyone else: [today is Labor Day and the midterm sprint starts now, so we are doing twenty-six percent off for 2026. 48 hours. It ends at 11:59 Tuesday Eastern and it does not come back.](https://substack.com/redirect/846461a1-d021-4b27-9444-fc598db38b6c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

That is less than four dollars a month for all six of those, plus everything that runs between now and November, plus the archive, plus the comment threads where the sharpest people I know argue with each other and occasionally with me. body:
You deserve to know why I’m asking Virginians to re-hire me, and why I decided to run for office in the first place.

---
| | | | _Peter, this is a longer email than I normally send, but it’s deeply personal to me. I know I ask for your support often, and you deserve to know why I’m asking Virginians to re-hire me, and why I decided to run for office in the first place._
---
[_**_If you’re short on time and already with me in the fight, then please consider a contribution split between my campaign and Governor Spanberger's United for Virginia's Future Federal PAC >>_**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138812611/645275392/-1439479448?refcode=BLU_EM_UFVF_2026-09-08_01&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjQvMS8xMDM4NTgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYmQ3MGZiYWYtYmJhYi1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5MzNiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=AUZF239UbQmuTW1qPy-1vbSxiRPmCu7761B7Zuem2to=)
| |
---
| | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138812612/645275393/-1439479448?refcode=BLU_EM_UFVF_2026-09-08_01&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjQvMS8xMDM4NTgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYmQ3MGZiYWYtYmJhYi1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5MzNiIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=AUZF239UbQmuTW1qPy-1vbSxiRPmCu7761B7Zuem2to=)
---
| | | **I first ran for public office for two reasons. First, because I believe that every Virginian – and every American – should have the same shot at success that I had.**
---
I grew up in a middle class family, went to public school, and was the first in my family to graduate from college.
I then tried to get into business, and failed in about six weeks. My next attempt failed in six months. I was incredibly fortunate that my third venture broke through, and that I continued to see success throughout my career in the telecommunications industry.
Success should _never_ depend on where you were born, who your parents are, or whether you had the right connections.
**Second, I got into politics because I believe you shouldn’t have to leave your hometown to find a world class job.** Success cannot depend on luck or geography. You should be able to build a good life in any zip code in Virginia.
It all comes down to this: Where you start should never determine where you end up. And it’s not lost on me – we’ve got a lot more work to do to make that a reality.
