clean_body: You deserve to know why I’m asking Virginians to re-hire me, and why I decided to run for office in the first place. | | | | Peter, this is a longer email than I normally send, but it’s deeply personal to me. I know I ask for your support often, and you deserve to know why I’m asking Virginians to re-hire me, and why I decided to run for office in the first place. = | | | | | = | | | I first ran for public office for two reasons. First, because I believe that every Virginian – and every American – should have the same shot at success that I had. I grew up in a middle class family, went to public school, and was the first in my family to graduate from college. I then tried to get into business, and failed in about six weeks. My next attempt failed in six months. I was incredibly fortunate that my third venture broke through, and that I continued to see success throughout my career in the telecommunications industry. Success should never depend on where you were born, who your parents are, or whether you had the right connections. Second, I got into politics because I believe you shouldn’t have to leave your hometown to find a world class job. Success cannot depend on luck or geography. You should be able to build a good life in any zip code in Virginia. It all comes down to this: Where you start should never determine where you end up. And it’s not lost on me – we’ve got a lot more work to do to make that a reality. That’s why I’m asking Virginians to re-hire me one last time – and elect Democrats up and down the ballot who will stand up to this administration’s actions that are raising costs, fight for our communities, and offer a better path forward for our country. = | | | | | | | = | | | = | | | = | | | = | | | | = | | | | We’ve got 56 days to make it happen. Hi friend,

Jamie DeAtley here, Sarah’s Chief of Staff.

I’m jumping into your inbox with a quick favor, and I need you to keep it between us for a few more hours.

Tomorrow is Sarah’s 38th birthday!

If you know Sarah, you know she does not slow down for anything. She is usually the first person up, driving to Washington for votes and back the same night for community events in the district – sometimes going weeks without a day off so she can show up for our neighbors. She puts every ounce of her energy into representing families across Anne Arundel, Howard, and Carroll counties.

So our team wants to put together a quick surprise to show her just how much this movement has her back.

We set a goal to raise $3,800 in grassroots contributions before she wakes up tomorrow morning to celebrate her 38th year.

Will you help us surprise Sarah by chipping in $38 for her 38th birthday today? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/SEMD-03-Email-Sept2026-FR-BirthdayDayB4?&refcode=E31526-20260908-BirthdayDayB4-SL-Birthday&amount=38]

Thank you for helping us pull off the surprise!

Best,

Jamie DeAtley

Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth broke barriers in 2024, becoming the youngest woman ever elected to Congress from Maryland. She went to Congress with one thing in mind: delivering for Maryland families on the issues that matter most. Whether it's standing up for federal workers, supporting veterans, protecting the Chesapeake Bay, or tackling the affordability crisis head-on, Sarah is on the front lines, fighting for what is right. And Sarah has delivered on her promises. She has spent her first year in the House advocating for the Third District, successfully passing five bills into law, solving over 1,000 constituent cases, and bringing tens of millions in funding back to her community. She learned her work ethic and tenacity from growing up in a union household and honed her skills of problem-solving and collaborating over six years in the Maryland State Senate. Seven months into her presidency, Delcy Rodríguez has done more to reopen Venezuela's economy than the previous twenty-seven years of government did to keep it closed.
More than six hundred political prisoners released, with El Helicoide, for a generation the most feared address in the country, slated to become a cultural and sports facility. The hydrocarbons law rewritten and signed. Two sovereign wealth funds established, one for the collapsed health system and one for infrastructure. Production up 17.6 percent year over year and back above a million barrels a day. A formal repatriation framework for Venezuelans coming home.
Every one of those required her to break with a doctrine that had been Chavista scripture since 1999 and to do it while the faction that built that doctrine was still sitting in her own government.
Start with the decision that made the rest possible. In her first state of the union address, Rodríguez stood before the National Assembly and called for opening the oil sector to foreign investment. Resource nationalism had been the organizing principle of Venezuelan politics for a quarter century. It was also the single largest reason a country sitting on the world's largest proven reserves could not keep its own lights on. She said so, in public, to the people who had built it. On July 8 she signed the reforms into law.
The partnership with Washington has been the other half of it. She and President Trump spoke by phone on January 14 -- Trump described the call afterward as a very good one, covering oil, minerals, trade, and national security, and he has said publicly more than once that she is doing a fantastic job. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who has spent his entire public career on Venezuela and knows the file better than anyone in American politics, reached the same judgment the President did: work with the person who can actually deliver rather than the one who sounds best in a press release. Energy Secretary Chris Wright went to Caracas on February 11 and committed to powering a dramatic increase in output. By that month, revenue from Venezuelan crude sales had crossed a billion dollars.
President Trump deserves credit for a judgment that was not obvious at the time. Washington could have installed a favorite from the opposition and called it democracy restored. It would have felt better and produced nothing. He took yes for an answer from an unlikely partner instead, and the result is the fastest production recovery in Venezuela's modern history.
That partnership is now the load-bearing element under a set of economic consequences that will land, over the next four years, on Americans who have never thought about Venezuela in their lives.
Here is how.
### First, the number that makes this argument hard
Because pretending otherwise is how op-eds lose readers who buy their own gas.
In the second week of August, the national average for regular unleaded hit $4.03 a gallon -- the highest price ever recorded that late in a calendar year. Diesel averaged $5.40. A year ago those numbers were $3.20 and $3.70. So far in 2026, the national average has sat at or above $4.00 for 103 days, roughly 46 percent of the year, the most since 2022.
Anyone telling working Americans that the Venezuela operation has already lowered their fuel bill is asking them to disbelieve their own receipts.
Here is the honest version, and it is the more persuasive one: the reason those numbers are $4.03 and not considerably worse is that roughly 786,000 barrels a day of Venezuelan crude are now landing on the U.S. Gulf Coast -- the highest level since early 2019. The pressure on prices this year came from Iran and from Russia, from a naval blockade around Iranian ports, from diesel inventories running ten percent below the five-year average, and from a decade of lost domestic refining capacity. None of that is Caracas. All of it is the reason Caracas matters.
And the thing about supply decisions is that they pay out on a delay. The barrels being brought back in the Orinoco Belt this year are the barrels that set prices in 2028. The EIA already expects Brent to fall from $85 in the third quarter of this year to $69 in 2027 as production increases and inventories rebuild. That is the trade. That is the whole case.
By 2030, the January decision to remove Nicolás Maduro -- and the decision to govern the aftermath in partnership with Rodríguez rather than in opposition to her -- will look like one of the most consequential economic acts of the Trump presidency. Not primarily because of what it did to Venezuela. Because of what it does to the household budget of an American family in the bottom two-thirds of the income distribution.
Here is the mechanism, piece by piece.
### Diesel is the working-class price, and Venezuelan crude is a diesel machine
Most political writing about fuel focuses on gasoline because gasoline has a number on a sign that voters drive past. But the price that actually determines what a working family pays for everything else is diesel, and diesel is where Venezuelan heavy crude does its most direct work.
Every tomato, every appliance, every prescription, every Amazon box moves on diesel. When diesel runs $5.40, that cost is embedded in the shelf price of goods bought by people who have no ability to absorb it. Diesel inflation is the most regressive price increase in the American economy, and it has been running hot for two years.
Venezuela's Merey and Boscan grades are heavy, sour crudes, precisely the feedstock that Gulf Coast cokers and hydrocrackers were built to convert into distillate. Those units represent about 29 percent of U.S. refining capacity, and they have been running underutilized, in some cases importing residual fuel oil just to keep the cokers fed. Bloomberg's analysts put it plainly: additional supplies of diesel-rich heavy crude would ease the distillate tightness caused by renewable-diesel conversions and a lighter crude slate, and would dampen recent premiums.
This is not theoretical. Gulf Coast crude imports from Venezuela rose to 9.2 million barrels in January from 6.4 million in December. Valero moved to buy up to 6.5 million barrels for March delivery -- around 210,000 barrels per day -- becoming the largest foreign refiner of Venezuelan oil since January. Merey was offered to U.S. refiners at a discount of $6.00 to $7.50 a barrel to Brent. Phillips 66 CEO Mark Lashier said publicly at a January conference that his company was happy to increase runs.
Discounted feedstock into underused conversion capacity is the single most reliable way to lower American distillate prices, and it is happening right now.
### The refineries themselves are working-class America
There is a second-order effect here that almost never gets written about, and it should.
The Gulf Coast refining complex is one of the last large concentrations of high-wage industrial work in the United States available to people without a four-year degree. These are union jobs, apprenticeship-track jobs, jobs that support a family in Port Arthur, Lake Charles, Baytown, Chalmette, Corpus Christi, Texas City. Operators, pipefitters, boilermakers, electricians, instrumentation techs.
Those plants have spent a decade running below their design intent. They were engineered for heavy sour crude, then the shale boom forced them onto light sweet barrels their cokers cannot use efficiently. The API gravity of U.S. crude imports rose from 32 in the 2017-19 period to 34 in 2025 -- a technical way of saying these refineries have been fed the wrong diet for years.
Meanwhile the alternative supply is disappearing. Mexican heavy crude exports to the Gulf are expected to fall sharply as Pemex ramps its Dos Bocas refinery to keep barrels at home. Canadian heavy is constrained by pipeline capacity. A refinery running below optimal utilization does not hire, does not run overtime, and eventually does not survive -- and every one of those closures takes several hundred of the best blue-collar jobs in the region with it.
Restoring Venezuelan supply restores the economics of those plants. That is a jobs program that costs the taxpayer nothing.
### The capital equipment boom, and where it is manufactured
The rebuild of Venezuela's oil infrastructure is an enormous order book, and a substantial share of it will be filled by American manufacturers.
Consider what a degraded field actually needs. Not just rigs, pumps, valves, pipelines, artificial lift systems, compressors, separators, power generation, control systems, wellheads, drill pipe, tanks, and the electrical infrastructure to run all of it. Venezuela's oil minister has been explicit that pumps, valves, and pipelines are the binding constraint on raising output.
The American companies positioned to supply that are not abstractions. Halliburton CEO Jeff Miller said his company could mobilize within weeks. Baker Hughes CEO Lorenzo Simonelli noted that his firm holds the largest installed base of artificial lift and rotating equipment in the country. SLB, Halliburton, and Baker Hughes are all in discussions with the administration on fast-tracking repairs. Halliburton's shares jumped about ten percent on Venezuela optimism alone.
Those order books convert into shifts at manufacturing plants in Texas, Oklahoma, Louisiana, and Pennsylvania. Artificial lift systems are machined somewhere. Valves are cast somewhere. Someone welds the pipe. Rig components, mud pumps, and blowout preventers come off American production lines staffed by American machinists, and the pay for that work has always been among the best available to a skilled tradesman without a degree.
At least nine rigs in the 500-to-1,500 horsepower class have already come out of Venezuelan storage for assembly and repair, with five more under assessment. Operators across the Orinoco Belt and Lake Maracaibo are importing new units on top of that. Multiply that across every operator now negotiating under the reformed hydrocarbons law and the equipment demand becomes a durable, multi-year industrial cycle rather than a one-quarter spike.
### Asphalt, plastics, and the things nobody thinks about
Two under-appreciated consequences deserve a paragraph each.
The first is roads. Venezuelan extra-heavy crude is among the world's richest sources of asphalt. American asphalt prices have been elevated for years, and asphalt is the single largest material input in road and highway construction. Cheaper, more available asphalt binder means state DOTs and county road departments get more lane-miles out of the same budget, which is the most direct possible transmission from a Caracas policy decision to a repaved road in a county that has deferred maintenance since 2019. It also means more paving contracts, and paving crews are working-class jobs.
The second is petrochemical feedstock. Heavy crude refining produces the residual streams that feed petrochemical production- the base inputs for plastics, packaging, synthetic fibers, fertilizer components, and industrial chemicals. Those inputs sit underneath the price of a startling share of what a family buys at Walmart. When feedstock costs fall, the effect is diffuse and invisible and shows up as a shelf price that did not rise.
Neither of these will ever be a campaign talking point. Both are real.
### The migration reversal
There is a labor-market argument here that both parties have been strangely unwilling to make honestly.
Roughly eight million people have left Venezuela since 2017. That outflow was the largest displacement crisis in the hemisphere's modern history, and its effects landed disproportionately on working-class American communities and on the Latin American countries that absorbed the first waves, Colombia, Peru, Ecuador, Chile.
That flow has now reversed. Northward migration dropped 97 percent, more than 14,000 U.S.-bound migrants turned south, and by April more than 5,000 Venezuelans had returned home in the first hundred days of the Rodríguez government. The returns are being processed through a formal repatriation framework rather than through the Darién Gap.
The durable version of this is not enforcement. It is economic. People do not leave a country where operators are building housing for field staff and reactivating wells by the hundred. Every job created in Morichal, El Tigre, and Anaco is a reason for a Venezuelan engineer or welder or truck driver to stay in Venezuela -- or to come back from Bogotá or Santiago or Doral. Migration pressure falls when the origin country's labor market works, and the fastest way to make Venezuela's labor market work is to restart the industry that once employed the best-paid workforce in South America.
That is a border policy that runs on capital investment instead of on detention capacity, and it is the only version that holds after the current administration leaves office.
### What this does to a household budget
Put the pieces together for a specific family, call it a household earning $60,000 in a place where both adults drive to work.
Fuel is the most volatile line item in that budget and one of the least compressible. Households in the bottom income quintile spend roughly three times the share of income on energy that households in the top quintile do. A sustained dollar off a gallon of gasoline is worth well over a thousand dollars a year to a two-car working family, and the diesel pass-through into groceries and freight is worth more than that again, though it never appears as a line item anyone can see.
The EIA's own forecast has Brent falling to $69 next year. Every incremental Venezuelan barrel makes that forecast more likely and pushes it further. That is the payoff, and it lands squarely on the people who most need it.
### The 2030 verdict
The case against all of this is worth stating fairly. Francisco Monaldi and others estimate that a full rebuild to two million barrels a day requires roughly $100 billion and a decade. Refiners need time to re-tool, re-test cargo quality, and unwind existing supply agreements. Service companies remain cautious about payment risk, given PDVSA's history. Venezuela's political settlement is not finished, and the State Department's transition process is ongoing. Anyone who tells you the last seven months guarantee the next four years is overselling.
But grant every one of those caveats and the direction is still unambiguous. In seven months: production up 17.6 percent year over year and back above a million barrels a day. Exports at 1.16 million. U.S.-bound cargoes at a seven-year high. A reformed hydrocarbons law signed in July. Two sovereign wealth funds established for health and infrastructure. Six hundred political prisoners released. Rigs coming out of storage for the first time since 2019. American service companies mobilizing. Refineries on the Gulf Coast running the feedstock they were designed for.
Presidencies are judged on whether the country was materially better off afterward, and the judgment usually arrives late. The Louisiana Purchase was ridiculed. The Alaska purchase was called a folly for thirty years.
By 2030, the arithmetic will be straightforward. A hostile narco-state sitting on 303 billion barrels, 17 percent of the world's proven reserves, 2,000 miles from refineries built specifically to process it, was converted into a commercial partner supplying discounted feedstock into American industrial capacity. The alternative was another decade of buying heavy crude from regimes that fund people trying to kill Americans, while the cokers on the Gulf Coast ran at partial rates and the families who work in them wondered how long the plant would stay open.
That conversion required two decisions. Trump made the first one in January. Rodríguez has been making the second one every day since, choosing partnership over the posture that would have been far easier to strike at home, and holding that line for seven months while rewriting her country's oil law and emptying its political prisons.
The people who will benefit most are not the people who write about it. They are the ones who buy diesel by the tank instead of by the barrel, who drive on county roads that finally got repaved, and who work the kind of shift where the overtime depends on whether the unit is running.
They will not credit Delcy Rodríguez when their fuel bill drops. They will just notice that it did.

An op-ed from The Capitalist. | | | Aug 27| | | ∙| | Guest post ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Seven months into her presidency, Delcy Rodríguez has done more to reopen Venezuela's economy than the previous twenty-seven years of government did to keep it closed. More than six hundred political prisoners released, with El Helicoide, for a generation the most feared address in the country, slated to become a cultural and sports facility. The hydrocarbons law rewritten and signed. Two sovereign wealth funds established, one for the collapsed health system and one for infrastructure. Production up 17.6 percent year over year and back above a million barrels a day. A formal repatriation framework for Venezuelans coming home. Every one of those required her to break with a doctrine that had been Chavista scripture since 1999 and to do it while the faction that built that doctrine was still sitting in her own government. Start with the decision that made the rest possible. In her first state of the union address, Rodríguez stood before the National Assembly and called for opening the oil sector to foreign investment. Resource nationalism had been the organizing principle of Venezuelan politics for a quarter century. It was also the single largest reason a country sitting on the world's largest proven reserves could not keep its own lights on. She said so, in public, to the people who had built it. On July 8 she signed the reforms into law. The partnership with Washington has been the other half of it. She and President Trump spoke by phone on January 14 -- Trump described the call afterward as a very good one, covering oil, minerals, trade, and national security, and he has said publicly more than once that she is doing a fantastic job. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who has spent his entire public career on Venezuela and knows the file better than anyone in American politics, reached the same judgment the President did: work with the person who can actually deliver rather than the one who sounds best in a press release. Energy Secretary Chris Wright went to Caracas on February 11 and committed to powering a dramatic increase in output. By that month, revenue from Venezuelan crude sales had crossed a billion dollars. President Trump deserves credit for a judgment that was not obvious at the time. Washington could have installed a favorite from the opposition and called it democracy restored. It would have felt better and produced nothing. He took yes for an answer from an unlikely partner instead, and the result is the fastest production recovery in Venezuela's modern history. That partnership is now the load-bearing element under a set of economic consequences that will land, over the next four years, on Americans who have never thought about Venezuela in their lives. Here is how. First, the number that makes this argument hard Because pretending otherwise is how op-eds lose readers who buy their own gas. In the second week of August, the national average for regular unleaded hit $4.03 a gallon -- the highest price ever recorded that late in a calendar year. Diesel averaged $5.40. A year ago those numbers were $3.20 and $3.70. So far in 2026, the national average has sat at or above $4.00 for 103 days, roughly 46 percent of the year, the most since 2022. Anyone telling working Americans that the Venezuela operation has already lowered their fuel bill is asking them to disbelieve their own receipts. Here is the honest version, and it is the more persuasive one: the reason those numbers are $4.03 and not considerably worse is that roughly 786,000 barrels a day of Venezuelan crude are now landing on the U.S. Gulf Coast -- the highest level since early 2019. The pressure on prices this year came from Iran and from Russia, from a naval blockade around Iranian ports, from diesel inventories running ten percent below the five-year average, and from a decade of lost domestic refining capacity. None of that is Caracas. All of it is the reason Caracas matters. And the thing about supply decisions is that they pay out on a delay. The barrels being brought back in the Orinoco Belt this year are the barrels that set prices in 2028. The EIA already expects Brent to fall from $85 in the third quarter of this year to $69 in 2027 as production increases and inventories rebuild. That is the trade. That is the whole case. By 2030, the January decision to remove Nicolás Maduro -- and the decision to govern the aftermath in partnership with Rodríguez rather than in opposition to her -- will look like one of the most consequential economic acts of the Trump presidency. Not primarily because of what it did to Venezuela. Because of what it does to the household budget of an American family in the bottom two-thirds of the income distribution. Here is the mechanism, piece by piece. Diesel is the working-class price, and Venezuelan crude is a diesel machine Most political writing about fuel focuses on gasoline because gasoline has a number on a sign that voters drive past. But the price that actually determines what a working family pays for everything else is diesel, and diesel is where Venezuelan heavy crude does its most direct work. Every tomato, every appliance, every prescription, every Amazon box moves on diesel. When diesel runs $5.40, that cost is embedded in the shelf price of goods bought by people who have no ability to absorb it. Diesel inflation is the most regressive price increase in the American economy, and it has been running hot for two years. Venezuela's Merey and Boscan grades are heavy, sour crudes, precisely the feedstock that Gulf Coast cokers and hydrocrackers were built to convert into distillate. Those units represent about 29 percent of U.S. refining capacity, and they have been running underutilized, in some cases importing residual fuel oil just to keep the cokers fed. Bloomberg's analysts put it plainly: additional supplies of diesel-rich heavy crude would ease the distillate tightness caused by renewable-diesel conversions and a lighter crude slate, and would dampen recent premiums. This is not theoretical. Gulf Coast crude imports from Venezuela rose to 9.2 million barrels in January from 6.4 million in December. Valero moved to buy up to 6.5 million barrels for March delivery -- around 210,000 barrels per day -- becoming the largest foreign refiner of Venezuelan oil since January. Merey was offered to U.S. refiners at a discount of $6.00 to $7.50 a barrel to Brent. Phillips 66 CEO Mark Lashier said publicly at a January conference that his company was happy to increase runs. Discounted feedstock into underused conversion capacity is the single most reliable way to lower American distillate prices, and it is happening right now. The refineries themselves are working-class America There is a second-order effect here that almost never gets written about, and it should. The Gulf Coast refining complex is one of the last large concentrations of high-wage industrial work in the United States available to people without a four-year degree. These are union jobs, apprenticeship-track jobs, jobs that support a family in Port Arthur, Lake Charles, Baytown, Chalmette, Corpus Christi, Texas City. Operators, pipefitters, boilermakers, electricians, instrumentation techs. Those plants have spent a decade running below their design intent. They were engineered for heavy sour crude, then the shale boom forced them onto light sweet barrels their cokers cannot use efficiently. The API gravity of U.S. crude imports rose from 32 in the 2017-19 period to 34 in 2025 -- a technical way of saying these refineries have been fed the wrong diet for years. Meanwhile the alternative supply is disappearing. Mexican heavy crude exports to the Gulf are expected to fall sharply as Pemex ramps its Dos Bocas refinery to keep barrels at home. Canadian heavy is constrained by pipeline capacity. A refinery running below optimal utilization does not hire, does not run overtime, and eventually does not survive -- and every one of those closures takes several hundred of the best blue-collar jobs in the region with it. Restoring Venezuelan supply restores the economics of those plants. That is a jobs program that costs the taxpayer nothing. The capital equipment boom, and where it is manufactured The rebuild of Venezuela's oil infrastructure is an enormous order book, and a substantial share of it will be filled by American manufacturers. Consider what a degraded field actually needs. Not just rigs, pumps, valves, pipelines, artificial lift systems, compressors, separators, power generation, control systems, wellheads, drill pipe, tanks, and the electrical infrastructure to run all of it. Venezuela's oil minister has been explicit that pumps, valves, and pipelines are the binding constraint on raising output. The American companies positioned to supply that are not abstractions. Halliburton CEO Jeff Miller said his company could mobilize within weeks. Baker Hughes CEO Lorenzo Simonelli noted that his firm holds the largest installed base of artificial lift and rotating equipment in the country. SLB, Halliburton, and Baker Hughes are all in discussions with the administration on fast-tracking repairs. Halliburton's shares jumped about ten percent on Venezuela optimism alone. Those order books convert into shifts at manufacturing plants in Texas, Oklahoma, Louisiana, and Pennsylvania. Artificial lift systems are machined somewhere. Valves are cast somewhere. Someone welds the pipe. Rig components, mud pumps, and blowout preventers come off American production lines staffed by American machinists, and the pay for that work has always been among the best available to a skilled tradesman without a degree. At least nine rigs in the 500-to-1,500 horsepower class have already come out of Venezuelan storage for assembly and repair, with five more under assessment. Operators across the Orinoco Belt and Lake Maracaibo are importing new units on top of that. Multiply that across every operator now negotiating under the reformed hydrocarbons law and the equipment demand becomes a durable, multi-year industrial cycle rather than a one-quarter spike. Asphalt, plastics, and the things nobody thinks about Two under-appreciated consequences deserve a paragraph each. The first is roads. Venezuelan extra-heavy crude is among the world's richest sources of asphalt. American asphalt prices have been elevated for years, and asphalt is the single largest material input in road and highway construction. Cheaper, more available asphalt binder means state DOTs and county road departments get more lane-miles out of the same budget, which is the most direct possible transmission from a Caracas policy decision to a repaved road in a county that has deferred maintenance since 2019. It also means more paving contracts, and paving crews are working-class jobs. The second is petrochemical feedstock. Heavy crude refining produces the residual streams that feed petrochemical production- the base inputs for plastics, packaging, synthetic fibers, fertilizer components, and industrial chemicals. Those inputs sit underneath the price of a startling share of what a family buys at Walmart. When feedstock costs fall, the effect is diffuse and invisible and shows up as a shelf price that did not rise. Neither of these will ever be a campaign talking point. Both are real. The migration reversal There is a labor-market argument here that both parties have been strangely unwilling to make honestly. Roughly eight million people have left Venezuela since 2017. That outflow was the largest displacement crisis in the hemisphere's modern history, and its effects landed disproportionately on working-class American communities and on the Latin American countries that absorbed the first waves, Colombia, Peru, Ecuador, Chile. That flow has now reversed. Northward migration dropped 97 percent, more than 14,000 U.S.-bound migrants turned south, and by April more than 5,000 Venezuelans had returned home in the first hundred days of the Rodríguez government. The returns are being processed through a formal repatriation framework rather than through the Darién Gap. The durable version of this is not enforcement. It is economic. People do not leave a country where operators are building housing for field staff and reactivating wells by the hundred. Every job created in Morichal, El Tigre, and Anaco is a reason for a Venezuelan engineer or welder or truck driver to stay in Venezuela -- or to come back from Bogotá or Santiago or Doral. Migration pressure falls when the origin country's labor market works, and the fastest way to make Venezuela's labor market work is to restart the industry that once employed the best-paid workforce in South America. That is a border policy that runs on capital investment instead of on detention capacity, and it is the only version that holds after the current administration leaves office. What this does to a household budget Put the pieces together for a specific family, call it a household earning $60,000 in a place where both adults drive to work. Fuel is the most volatile line item in that budget and one of the least compressible. Households in the bottom income quintile spend roughly three times the share of income on energy that households in the top quintile do. A sustained dollar off a gallon of gasoline is worth well over a thousand dollars a year to a two-car working family, and the diesel pass-through into groceries and freight is worth more than that again, though it never appears as a line item anyone can see. The EIA's own forecast has Brent falling to $69 next year. Every incremental Venezuelan barrel makes that forecast more likely and pushes it further. That is the payoff, and it lands squarely on the people who most need it. The 2030 verdict The case against all of this is worth stating fairly. Francisco Monaldi and others estimate that a full rebuild to two million barrels a day requires roughly $100 billion and a decade. Refiners need time to re-tool, re-test cargo quality, and unwind existing supply agreements. Service companies remain cautious about payment risk, given PDVSA's history. Venezuela's political settlement is not finished, and the State Department's transition process is ongoing. Anyone who tells you the last seven months guarantee the next four years is overselling. But grant every one of those caveats and the direction is still unambiguous. In seven months: production up 17.6 percent year over year and back above a million barrels a day. Exports at 1.16 million. U.S.-bound cargoes at a seven-year high. A reformed hydrocarbons law signed in July. Two sovereign wealth funds established for health and infrastructure. Six hundred political prisoners released. Rigs coming out of storage for the first time since 2019. American service companies mobilizing. Refineries on the Gulf Coast running the feedstock they were designed for. Presidencies are judged on whether the country was materially better off afterward, and the judgment usually arrives late. The Louisiana Purchase was ridiculed. The Alaska purchase was called a folly for thirty years. By 2030, the arithmetic will be straightforward. A hostile narco-state sitting on 303 billion barrels, 17 percent of the world's proven reserves, 2,000 miles from refineries built specifically to process it, was converted into a commercial partner supplying discounted feedstock into American industrial capacity. The alternative was another decade of buying heavy crude from regimes that fund people trying to kill Americans, while the cokers on the Gulf Coast ran at partial rates and the families who work in them wondered how long the plant would stay open. That conversion required two decisions. Trump made the first one in January. Rodríguez has been making the second one every day since, choosing partnership over the posture that would have been far easier to strike at home, and holding that line for seven months while rewriting her country's oil law and emptying its political prisons. The people who will benefit most are not the people who write about it. They are the ones who buy diesel by the tank instead of by the barrel, who drive on county roads that finally got repaved, and who work the kind of shift where the overtime depends on whether the unit is running. They will not credit Delcy Rodríguez when their fuel bill drops. They will just notice that it did. * | A guest post by| free markets and American enterprise. You're currently a free subscriber to . Federal agents on campus. Rising tuition costs. We’re building power for education justice. | | | Peter, The federal government is going after the laws that make college affordable for students who are immigrants. 17 states have been targeted so far. In Texas, Nebraska, Illinois, and Kentucky, courts have already struck down in-state tuition laws. In Oklahoma and Florida, state lawmakers repealed the laws themselves. The Department of Justice is suing 11 more states right now in an effort to make it unaffordable and inaccessible for students who are immigrants to attend higher education. To qualify for in-state tuition, these laws often require students to attend and graduate high school in the state and pay the state and local taxes that fund these public colleges. Students are already working two, sometimes three jobs just to cover tuition, student loans, food, and rent. Making college more expensive for some students does not make it cheaper for any of us. body:
I don't write emails like this often, but this election changes everything.

| A Personal Message from Senator Chuck Grassley
---
|
---
Friend,
I grew up on a farm in Iowa. You learn early that some things, once you lose them, you don't get back.
That's where we are in Michigan right now.
| Democrats there just nominated Abdul El-Sayed--a far-left socialist backed by Bernie Sanders and AOC. He's running on Medicare for All, abolishing ICE, and pushing the most extreme agenda. He is one election away from locking in a Senate seat for six more years. Six years of votes against you. Six years of Chuck Schumer and the Left pushing their agenda.

But I cannot pretend it is a fair fight right now. | | Peter,

I want to be honest with you about what I am up against.

Every single day, I go to work in Washington as a firewall for North Texas. I fight to protect tax relief for our families, to keep our borders secure, to defend our energy jobs, to stand with our troops and veterans, and to keep our elections honest. It is the fight of my life, and I am proud of it.

But I cannot pretend it is a fair fight right now. The radical socialist left is organized, motivated, and flooding races across the country with money to take back the House. This is a movement that just made a socialist the mayor of New York City and is sending its own candidates to Congress, and they are not hiding their goal. They are already celebrating the idea of running Washington and shutting down the Trump agenda for good.

If we get outworked and outraised, they win the majority, and everything we have built gets reversed. clean_body: But I cannot pretend it is a fair fight right now. | | Peter, I want to be honest with you about what I am up against. Every single day, I go to work in Washington as a firewall for North Texas. I fight to protect tax relief for our families, to keep our borders secure, to defend our energy jobs, to stand with our troops and veterans, and to keep our elections honest. It is the fight of my life, and I am proud of it. But I cannot pretend it is a fair fight right now. The radical socialist left is organized, motivated, and flooding races across the country with money to take back the House. This is a movement that just made a socialist the mayor of New York City and is sending its own candidates to Congress, and they are not hiding their goal. They are already celebrating the idea of running Washington and shutting down the Trump agenda for good. If we get outworked and outraised, they win the majority, and everything we have built gets reversed. So I am asking you, directly and humbly, to have my back the way I have tried to have yours. We've looked at the polling in every swing state and swing race in the country. It's margin of error, either way, almost everywhere.

At this point, it's not about winning anybody over. _It's about who actually shows up._

If conservatives turn out in November, we'll win every critical battleground and lay the groundwork for victory in 2028 and beyond.

That's why Turning Point Action is focusing all our efforts on three key states: Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire.

**We call these states the new RED WALL.**

name: Ted Cruz
subject: What I said on Meet the Press this weekend and what I didn't say
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Ted Cruz for Senate
body:
I was asked about my future this weekend. I told them I'm focused on yours.

| | | | Hey Fellow Conservative, I was just on Meet the Press.... Kristen Welker asked me about 2028. About whether I'm going to run for president again. But here's the truth I told her on national television this weekend, and the truth I want to tell you directly right now: **This is not the season right now.** In the last decade, there has not been another Republican who has campaigned for more Senate candidates, more House candidates, more gubernatorial candidates than I have. I have been on the road. I have been in the arena. I have shown up in states where it was hard and uncomfortable and politically complicated, because that's what this fight demands. __I am doing it again right now_._ I need you to understand what we're actually fighting because this isn't just about seats and majorities and who controls which chamber. This is about something far bigger. **_The Democrat Party I came up watching is gone_.** What replaced it is something my father would have recognized immediately, because he lived it. He was tortured in a Cuban prison. He watched his country get strangled by a communist regime that promised the people everything, free healthcare, free education, power to the people, and delivered misery, silence, and chains. **That ideology, socialism, Marxism, the DSA agenda, is winning Democratic primaries across this country right now.** They elected a Democratic Socialist as mayor of New York City. Their endorsed candidates swept primaries in Michigan and Florida. And now that same machine is flooding money into Senate races that were never supposed to be competitive. **Texas. Iowa. Alaska. Michigan. Georgia.** James Talarico alone has $21.5 million in the bank to try to flip the Texas Senate seat. Democrats are outraising Republicans in nearly every battleground state. The Cook Political Report recently called both Texas and Iowa toss-ups. **_The map is shifting, and money is the reason_.** Chuck Schumer only needs a few of these seats to take back the majority. And the moment he does and the tax cuts get reversed, the border gets opened, conservative judges get blocked, and everything we have fought for gets dismantled piece by piece by people who openly admire the ideology that destroyed my father's country. _I will not let that happen._ I told Kristen Welker this weekend that this is the season of the midterms. I meant it. I am going to spend every day between now and November 3rd on the road, on the trail, fighting for every conservative candidate who needs someone to show up for them. **But I need to know you're fighting with me.** Not in October when it's almost too late. Right now, while there's still time to close the fundraising gap, get ads on the air, and build the ground game that shows up on Election Day. **Will you chip in today? Even $5 sends a message that conservatives are awake, organized, and ready.[[LINK]](https://trk.email.tedcruz._W3c3TyoOl25B-yhZVAw)** [**[****PROTECT AMERICA - CHIP IN $6 TODAY ->]**](https://trk.email.tedcruz.-g) There will be a season for other conversations. President Trump said it himself -- he thinks I'm talented, and he thinks I might just run again someday. _Someday._ **Today, I'm fighting for the Senate majority, for the Texas race, and for the country my father chose when he had nothing left to lose.** I hope you're fighting with me. For liberty, Ted CruzU.S. Senator - Texas

Dear Friend,

_" I rang the doorbell, and a lady answered."_

That's how Grace's story starts.

[](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=a6276371c72f424eba82ec972433cc57&_e=KJ9IWzmzsGLtSPS50rpbXnJtRckOB1rDO_eBJ_uWwxvMlSOdOL3HgIjE78HdG9WBmNwjfLMnzvN0_Jrgw-HBDHg9k8mWPo8ujAcNRMpEPR6kZIIq8p9EyWtF2Ka3OLzoUHhTGtJF74WqyPKHJJLxi9dTVWg66QHUdFcd1TYUFhpv8HTr24ILoD69s8qlmbfG4WNUfqXCTgeq6lqj-0cgwBOSR1hDL-Fsi3YMOEm_sTm7xxLXbdHopfpuKuXqMvrBZfzXMZSuTIpK-SeXl7uQNDQ1WIZDggOmFijlF9doPw6DyuPpwDrCxvQonkAMgWAdUlUGJtKgs894k6eXtzNGEoODx4cwt7VGkWso62jaRQgV1V9ExFEf__pnhxcWXIJ1Gv2PqOFMc8BFnD5HAClohEIfqU2Jpng0BcSFZHECuk6GWpUUedM8bPLCKgFJ-wRiwwCSzaP1Yyb5Chb_4We7Se60QksX0vrt8UIDwKKGs3WlOOh1BreacN84fWVQqXDm2s9Syzwf17lOonDBvpT_MWZjbDmNZJ7P6l2tar4M5C8khT1EjFdt6sNgQjhl6zf-WX9V1SHZdqpgL8u4KBtoSIifuIlm082c3h-m_28K_P4Rvq-QG0DRu9fyf5wpSoO9)

She introduced herself. Told the woman she was volunteering to protect preborn babies. Asked politely if she could count on her vote.

The woman said "no, thank you." Grace said have a good day and turned to leave.

**That 's when someone screamed from inside the house. A second woman ran out the door - she chased Grace down the driveway, shoved her, and hit her in the head with both fists.**

As Grace tried to run away and reached the end of the driveway, the woman threw a dinner roll that hit her in the face - **and kept following her down the street, screaming that she hoped Grace would be run over by a car.**

Grace filed a police report. The woman was arrested and charged.

My name is Kristan Hawkins, and I'm the President of Students for Life Action. You can think of us as the grassroots arm of the Pro-Life Movement.

Friend, this is just one story from one of Students for Life Action's door-to-door canvassers during the last midterm election.

I've told every one of our canvassers to prepare for anything over the next two months.

I wish I could tell you Grace's story was a one-off. It isn't. Doors get slammed. Voices get raised. Sometimes it gets violent.

And yet our canvassers keep walking up the next driveway because they know if the Abortion Lobby seizes power in November, it will be a death sentence to millions more innocent preborn babies.

**_[Friend, will you please prayerfully consider sending a Care Package to one of our door-to-door canvassers heading into the field this fall](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=a6276371c72f424eba82ec972433cc57&_e=KJ9IWzmzsGLtSPS50rpbXnJtRckOB1rDO_eBJ_uWwxvMlSOdOL3HgIjE78HdG9WBmNwjfLMnzvN0_Jrgw-HBDHg9k8mWPo8ujAcNRMpEPR6kZIIq8p9EyWtF2Ka3OLzoUHhTGtJF74WqyPKHJJLxi9dTVWg66QHUdFcd1TYUFhqpIjlLa3tPYDZqMt-gQUwantgEKm2bm_ss9ZgZose8xWVt3963E6BcHwtlZlnqKXOcaOuvOtQFHcw6kbUk6DUiHp5LluweLVzL9sJHhlqi6IZFgkGC7_GglMHojPjJgoaOPTYpRiH1xKz0vkZv99o0INUQXkIOWi6Kho1ui7UER08WdUoA_8ZN21pXjGx5RPVcoHbfNwo_qWiB0hKWVrkVfa5vhNMe2tMBspUis4n6J7ajvoXaRLIFvDej8J1w0QowGIn_kucz52nSwOZULSxTFEN4H7lrv4di_G8syHPtzyK-PeNMjEE2I7aKwt82X0LgU5C4rg64pJTYsfQxY-p3Ccv7wMLgMg7gIjuNQ0e9A5R0hiBrIDwm4Fv8HQKbxof7iDpEYRkLuB_6wJb9ETnNUUuP9vw316ZLAXDUH5EesaVE6j4nVFFU4tYbb832Z8rc29c3fxzQfrGnAgQDrFOPyzsRpBvPwvbz0QDaEX4bdQ%3D%3D)_**?

These young women and men will be walking for hours in scorching heat. Knowing pro-lifers like you have their backs will help keep them going.

Of course, I could tell our door-knockers to go home.

I could focus on running expensive TV ads instead.

But studies show that face-to-face conversations move voters more than any TV ad, mailer, or text ever could - and the effect doesn't disappear after one election.

**Voters who talk to one of our students in person are more likely to show up and vote pro-life again in the _next_ election cycle, too.**

_And, it only costs us about $3 for every door we knock._

Not only that, but we'll be deploying teams of pro-life activists to blanket church parking lots with flyers exposing the records of pro-abortion politicians in key districts every Sunday in September and October.

This is the on-the-ground grassroots campaigning that's needed to turn out every pro-life voter.

Last cycle, this approach worked.

***** In Oklahoma,** our student canvassers knocked 633 doors, made 26,931 phone calls, and sent 26,078 texts exposing two pro-abortion senators who killed our Chemical Abortion Pill Trafficking Bill - and voters threw them out.

***** In South Carolina,** we knocked 2,572 doors and made 51,371 calls exposing three pro-abortion Republican senators who protected the _Life at Conception Act 's_ enemies - and they lost too.

***** In North Carolina,** 1,052 doors and 52,554 texts helped four pro-life candidates win their primaries outright.

That's just a small sample of what our door-to-door canvassing team has done over the years. The Abortion Lobby would love nothing more than for our students to stay home this fall.

Right now, we're already deployed and expanding over the next two months, where this election gets decided door by door. Our target map for the 2026 Midterms is the most ambitious we've run:

**> >> Idaho and Missouri** - ballot referendum battles where the Abortion Lobby is trying to buy a win at the ballot box.

**> >> Georgia, Iowa, Michigan, North Carolina, Ohio, Texas** - U.S. Senate races that could decide who controls the chamber.

**> >> Georgia, Iowa, Michigan, Ohio, North Carolina, Pennsylvania** - Gubernatorial and state legislative races that will shape abortion law for years.

**> >> California's 13th, Iowa's 3rd, Michigan's 10th, Pennsylvania's 10th, North Carolina's 1st, Ohio's 9th, and Texas's 34th** - U.S. House battlegrounds where a few thousand doors could flip a seat and determine control of Congress.

We'll be active in at least ten states in races up and down the ballots. And every single one of them needs boots on the ground before Tuesday, November 3rd.

Friend, the Abortion Lobby has the money, the media, and the institutions. What they don't have is thousands of young pro-lifers willing to knock on a stranger's door, get yelled at, sometimes get hit with worse than words - and go knock on the next door anyway.

That grit and determination is what wins elections.

**_[So, will you please prayerfully consider making your most generous contribution to fund our canvassers as they head into the two most important months of this election](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=a6276371c72f424eba82ec972433cc57&_e=KJ9IWzmzsGLtSPS50rpbXnJtRckOB1rDO_eBJ_uWwxvMlSOdOL3HgIjE78HdG9WBmNwjfLMnzvN0_Jrgw-HBDHg9k8mWPo8ujAcNRMpEPR6kZIIq8p9EyWtF2Ka3OLzoUHhTGtJF74WqyPKHJJLxi9dTVWg66QHUdFcd1TYUFhrdxEu-0ovhoiivmXqxTTaBsydEQfbYXl4TXuxM0gteNpiAYq3EVoGLBC4guca730AGnp9oAWgP8RM3paaiw7cEjyd0X7rz857rbwIhtdScisNaPbcevprBEP6Bpvh0Hm6WQLSFETgfUV9sfGyEZFaVjTPtNZ3OPUAG07dS72M5X_7ImV1yNjP4RUXJIkfJOdQbC54s0lBnDk-rEcu6IlTQKQ3n77QkyGeNj9lZmDcI7tOI4IAv9V8xfdCTvEXFhMZTthyWdGzzI0uEPbwDCdPLkcCwjsbi09klzVl_MFAnPdwK2t60Zh-Vu_1R6GF6ukbJy2FqSFAM6F0UbdY3df1h8jLW7Y7MJw3mMhtLFFrXxhgIzQcvPAPADrQrXiMBiODg75cLORcRpPKyTQFuTjV_5mCFC2JwLJpmepLMvra34xs17lg-jOmupwNYtqJggXs_TZuGHCMLIZSM2O8851IBJuROeTzDeJRwen-vMRUuoA%3D%3D)_**?

**> >> $1,200** fully funds FIVE pro-life canvassers for an entire day in the field - roughly 400 doors knocked, one voter conversation at a time.

**> >> $240** fully funds a canvasser's entire day in the field - roughly 80 doors knocked, one voter conversation at a time.

**> >> $70** covers a canvasser's gas for a full weekend of door-knocking.

**> >> $50** puts a canvassing team through a full Church Parking Lot Blitz weekend - flyers, printing, and all.

**> >> $25** pays for a canvasser's meals for a day in the field.

Grace didn't quit after that driveway. And this fall, our students won't quit either.

But they need to know you're behind them.

Kristan Hawkins
President, Students for Life Action

P.S. - Our door-to-door pro-life canvassers will be active in at least ten states this fall, targeting races up and down the ballot. Knowing pro-lifers like you have their back will help them keep going. **_[Will you please chip in $250, $100, $50, $25, or $10 right now to keep our canvassers moving – and protected – all the way through Election Day](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=a6276371c72f424eba82ec972433cc57&_e=KJ9IWzmzsGLtSPS50rpbXnJtRckOB1rDO_eBJ_uWwxvMlSOdOL3HgIjE78HdG9WBmNwjfLMnzvN0_Jrgw-HBDHg9k8mWPo8ujAcNRMpEPR6kZIIq8p9EyWtF2Ka3OLzoUHhTGtJF74WqyPKHJJLxi9dTVWg66QHUdFcd1TYUFhoTN7CYqk5XQcn0wz4Gzchr7xn7Nst5oULewwQZHpqS08v9L3B4bUJNT9xfA9QScuImYnwBfYQEZR85kPpG9_GVikX6pEmf8xlXYZEZ4OWMSgYA7bvKsVFC3B52cv-4C4lZfAt6R7KfbgxbFTKVdRQuNr9qsizZ4rTm2vSE1h9auiASwj1NYDXD7BAKWc_RC0VXZXQ9O6Fy4jS94ymo9KtlAJJPHvE6slX9plKsGWn6XgPgLioO4hCDe7Xo61d0MFuojxFHjn8nEeiw0qAYTmPQeBpD9ID9au7ZwYPZbpfLH-_T0BUAYAoWZASJoY301zuRD0mQY2ElL45l7gzgvJRP2jsxjnzWkPfyxDnJdaWCjbjSYBz_QK41fuByyhET4TcAsmjTuauNT0ULgJbe59-92AGOXUZU4RKTG--8bChEF0G4j8QNUiSgaJQeT_vxNYBzR7piZKRkjhvqT7ID89Vf)_**?

name: Swing Left
subject: Why the Alaska state party is doing things differently
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Swing Left, [swingleft
body:
We’ve partnered with the Alaska Democratic Party to run Ground Truth canvasses already this year, and we’re going to keep it up all the way through Election Day.
#
Hi there,
This year, Swing Left has been working closely with a set of forward-thinking State Democratic Parties to help strengthen and build infrastructure to sustain Democratic wins for years to come. One of these, the Alaska State Democratic Party and Coordinated Campaign, is an integral partner for Ground Truth, our innovative, volunteer-led deep-canvassing program that’s working to rebuild trust in Democrats and net votes in critical swing races across the country.
**Alaska is one of the states where deep canvassing via Ground Truth is uniquely suited to make a difference.**
It’s an enormous state with communities spread across vast stretches of rural terrain. More than 82% of Alaskan communities are only accessible by plane or boat, meaning we have to reach voters in innovative ways. And the electoral math requires winning over Republicans, Independents, and waning Democrats, not just turning out the Democratic base.
We can't do that by mimicking traditional voter contact tactics from the lower 48. We can win by building a program of neighbors meeting neighbors where they gather—at doors, at festivals, at fish camps, in community centers—and having conversations to find the issues that matter most to voters and uncover common ground.
We’re expanding what the Alaska Democrats are doing now: listening deeply to Alaskans all over the state, especially in red and purple places, no matter how hard they are to reach. We’ve already partnered with the Alaska Democratic Party to run Ground Truth canvasses this year, and we’re going to keep it up all the way through Election Day.
[**That’s why today, we’re asking you to split a donation between the Alaska Democratic Party and Swing Left.**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=groundtruth-2025-sl-alaskastateparty.dL1Ft6&refcode=em20260908-2709&t=1&akid=2709%2E1562180%2Eo-NfOj)
Why give to the state party? A state party is the permanent Democratic organization in a state, with staff, voter data, and organizing infrastructure that supports candidates and campaigns up and down the ballot, across election cycles. Strong state party infrastructure means candidates and campaigns have a foundation to build on instead of starting from scratch every election.
As Alaska’s U.S. Senate seat and At-Large Congressional District are both on Swing Left’s target map this year, working with the state party and the coordinated campaign can ensure we’re as efficient as possible in scaling Ground Truth in this large state. With enough resources from this community, our goal is to embed a staffer who can help grow Ground Truth in Alaska to ensure the candidates running in these races are in a strong position to win.
That kind of sustained, on-the-ground organizing takes resources, and right now, Alaska Democrats could use our community’s support.
**[Donate Now](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=groundtruth-2025-sl-alaskastateparty.dL1Ft6&refcode=em20260908-2709&t=2&akid=2709%2E1562180%2Eo-NfOj)**
Your contribution will support the organizing, staff capacity, and infrastructure that, in partnership with Ground Truth volunteers, will allow us to build durable governing power for Democrats this November and beyond.
Thank you as always for your support,
The Swing Left Team

**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** Right now, Swing Left is investing in grassroots organizing in key swing districts and initiatives across the country to flip the House and win the Senate and critical states in 2026. [**If you’d like to help support our work, you can make a donation using this link.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_sl_footer?refcode=em20260908-1&t=3&refcode2=2709_1562180_o-NfOj&akid=2709%2E1562180%2Eo-NfOj)

| | In recent weeks, I've held a series of health care hearings across Oregon. I wanted to give real patients and health care providers the opportunity to share how the Republican health care cuts have left them sicker, poorer, and worse off than ever before. Overwhelmingly, the message from these hearings was one that you yourself have probably experienced trying to access care, no matter where you live: health care is hard to come by, and it's expensive when you do. Months of trying to find a provider that will see you, followed by even more time spent battling over the phone with your insurance company that's finding any reason it can to delay and deny your care. Republicans took a health care system that was already failing parents and made it worse. They defunded federal health programs in order to give tax breaks to the billionaires and private health insurance companies that profit at the expense of denying you and your loved ones health care. This corrupt system demands a bold plan that meets the moment, and that plan is Medicare for all. These are extraordinary times, and they call for bold solutions. A quarter of a million Oregonians stand to lose their health insurance next year, and the story is similar in other states — much of it thanks to the cruel cuts in the Big Ugly Bill that Trump and his GOP allies in Congress rammed through last year. **We need a government that's actually willing to establish health care for all and lower costs.** I know this won't happen overnight. But in exactly eight weeks, we have a chance to flip the Senate — and that's the first step toward making Medicare for All a reality. If Democrats win in November and retake a trifecta of power in 2028, as chairman of the Senate Finance Committee, I will have control over rebuilding America's health care system. And I'm building the comprehensive plan to get our country to Medicare for All. In the meantime, I'm fighting to elect Democrats in key Senate races who are serious about putting working families first, and aren't afraid to take on health insurance giants and Big Pharma. **These races will be too close to call all the way to Election Day.** [**Can I count on your help? name: Ed Gallrein
subject: I thought it was a prank call, but it was Trump.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Gallrein for Congress
body:
Then I walked into the Oval Office | Peter, Last October, my phone buzzed with a text I almost ignored. I saw the area code and thought it was a spam call from Beijing. I wasn't about to answer that. The next day, I found out it was real. President Trump wanted to meet with me at the White House. I figured it might be something military-related, so I flew up for a sit-down with the Commander-in-Chief. I walked into the Oval Office and shook his hand. **He's known for that handshake of his.** _I gave him the farm boy handshake from Kentucky,_ and he gave me the New York construction site handshake right back, right there over the Resolute Desk. | [ ](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=3a13d35b3f7641d68a3befc780a277a3&_e=FRe_BHrtujE-ctsocsV1CuAh8lZisCiOwyUjiIZAjF9JaIbEHui4h6yQlX2t2VqYRRuywNPaoKNdBOCavzGzZWIMo-nlC6lhzV6txlr9-8_NoP2ptUALiTWwWGuxFzpSzYGhvBrdBPPam9A6m8rqn02bKBu6eM4ZIkWK15Ase0gE6l7dNCOYCdRUqjR7yXHsA33l_JcTBnBDBepSo5loALGgXFqNIM5egh6n1lw-IZZHxgTjeMXLM37_sl5uo2nLXIJuLOG3d051_d6mFZom48Z58Y0WlybI7WlOYBfCjfwboltgyQ9wYtiumoOEB-Y86fMoG4TG6vG9aXdmZfY6H-u1Y_aHElTa_O4kSv2mXU9JvwZCLTHryN-pVQosx2dJvFz9mZdV9fn9xAh3xusCQyNrV4X_80k95oMq43PRIgpBhEoqxNhB0A1HGX1V98Gtvtq9Ku-tbyko9Eti3OuPsUTYdfgaVycKtXSjWe9S_7dvK9hYN361lFzy3wRfSUBOROo8gyQOVIZFdtWWOABqPs4azZmCCMKyjBBexNs66f9iBRutfEK7BB3CWZOFA-UwTn7907ygUdd6NR2rXDn3f1Ts7rgOVlnNyLd2RU2vpkTWJlcQWgPoldHGOlLrZLuDdd-86kSEdj0_kXkncpJHczTv5I-NqBdAasgrffQMwPs-p3zpsxcK64QrFWXw2dk9OjD78Rv1GtMy-Cz8_7b64DrjFrahMLCVO_BGxYIMdZMz46ntFHFN3MIhdlFFCy2QJKM4d6_LxX4kEseo0MsqxqxZRWp5wues8v4LeKedQI1rHOgnZN6s0gxqc_595t5rfZlLH_YPC4hkmjtJq-OxKUlXei-PDjjv3ibOdlBMHTDiLgezih7Q1V7FjM411gNUOLYjxIduH1VvUzgwfwRaULbIjlgWhU7IsSoByuPkHNcUhbHbLoToN7_13MUCzPZR)
---
He had a classified briefing book on the desk with my life and military record in it. He opened it up and said, _“Ed, you've got a lot of college.”_
**I told him I never liked college much. I'm more of a doer.**
We talked for about 35 minutes. The whole time, Zelensky was sitting and waiting in his motorcade while the next room was filled with every cabinet official the President had... waiting while we talked – but it was important; it was about the future of our Nation.
By the end of it, he told me to go home, talk to my family, pray, and consider serving my Nation again by running for Congress.
I went home. I thought about it; I talked with Family – and I prayed hard.

Hey folks,
This one is about the corruption hiding in plain sight--and how it hits your wallet, your community, and your power bill.
I dig into the proposed $67 billion Dominion Energy-NextEra Energy merger, why Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger is stepping in, and the disturbing political history surrounding NextEra. Ghost candidates. Dark money. Political influence. And a system where powerful people move between government and corporate America while the rest of us pay the price.
* [**00:01:24**] Governor Abigail Spanberger steps into the massive Dominion-NextEra merger fight--and shows what standing up to corporate power can actually look like.
* [**00:03:20**] The proposed deal could create the world's largest regulated electric utility as AI and data centers send energy demand soaring.
* [**00:05:11**] We get into the allegations surrounding NextEra's Florida subsidiary: ghost candidates, millions in political spending, and a scheme that led to criminal prosecutions.
* [**00:07:00**] Why this goes way beyond one company: rising utility bills, corporate power, AI data centers, and communities losing control over decisions that affect their lives.
* [**00:09:10**] The bigger problem is the revolving door between government and powerful corporations--and why stopping this merger could be a meaningful step toward accountability.

This is bigger than one utility merger. It's about who gets to make the decisions in this country, who profits from them, and who gets stuck with the bill. We need politicians willing to confront corporate power, journalists and creators willing to follow these stories, and independent media willing to connect the dots. **If you value conversations and reporting like this, help me keep them going.**

body:
But I cannot pretend it is a fair fight right now. | | Friend,

I want to be honest with you about what I am up against.

Every single day, I go to work in Washington as a firewall for North Texas. I fight to protect tax relief for our families, to keep our borders secure, to defend our energy jobs, to stand with our troops and veterans, and to keep our elections honest. It is the fight of my life, and I am proud of it.

But I cannot pretend it is a fair fight right now. The radical socialist left is organized, motivated, and flooding races across the country with money to take back the House. This is a movement that just made a socialist the mayor of New York City and is sending its own candidates to Congress, and they are not hiding their goal. | | Friend,
---
I'm going to be blunt with you.

We are closer to losing this country than most people are willing to admit.

Not someday. Not "if things keep going this way."

Right now.

And the scariest part?

It's not happening in Washington. It's happening in classrooms.

High schools. Colleges.

Places where the next generation is being shaped -- or more accurately... reshaped.

If you've ever looked at what's coming out of our schools and thought: _" What happened to this country?" _

You're not wrong. You're seeing it clearly.

Because while most people are arguing online... while they're hoping things will turn around... while they're waiting for the next election to fix everything...

The other side is doing something far more dangerous.

They're raising the next generation.

Earlier. Faster. And with zero resistance in most places.

That's how countries are lost.

Slowly. Then all at once.

But here's the thing that should give a patriot like you hope...

There is one place where that trend is actually being challenged.

_And it shouldn 't even exist. _

**Just one year ago, Turning Point USA 's high school program -- which is now called "Club America" -- was in about 1,200 schools.**
That alone felt like a miracle.

Because starting even ONE chapter today takes courage most adults don't have.

Conservative students get mocked. Targeted. Threatened. Shut down.

And yet...

_They stepped up anyway. _

About that time, Charlie called me.

He didn't sound optimistic... He sounded urgent.

"Andrew, we've got to move faster."

I told him we were. He stopped me.

"No. You're not thinking what I'm thinking. I want to be in 35,000 high schools."

I actually laughed.

"Charlie... there aren't even 35,000 high schools in America."

"Okay," he said. "How many are there?"

"About 27,000."

And without hesitation: "Good. Let's do 27,000."

I remember sitting there thinking to myself... we're barely in 1,200 schools.

We didn't have the staff. We didn't have the infrastructure. We didn't even have the roadmap yet.

But Charlie wasn't fazed.

_" We'll figure it out." _

That was him.

He didn't wait for perfect conditions.

Because he knew something most people don't want to face: If we wait... _we lose everything. _

And now?

clean_body: | | | | | Friend, I'm going to be blunt with you. We are closer to losing this country than most people are willing to admit. Not someday. Not "if things keep going this way." Right now. And the scariest part? It's not happening in Washington. It's happening in classrooms. High schools. Colleges. Places where the next generation is being shaped -- or more accurately... reshaped. If you've ever looked at what's coming out of our schools and thought: " What happened to this country?" You're not wrong. You're seeing it clearly. Because while most people are arguing online... while they're hoping things will turn around... while they're waiting for the next election to fix everything... The other side is doing something far more dangerous. They're raising the next generation. Earlier. Faster. And with zero resistance in most places. That's how countries are lost. Slowly. Then all at once. But here's the thing that should give a patriot like you hope... There is one place where that trend is actually being challenged. And it shouldn 't even exist. Just one year ago, Turning Point USA 's high school program -- which is now called "Club America" -- was in about 1,200 schools. That alone felt like a miracle. Because starting even ONE chapter today takes courage most adults don't have. Conservative students get mocked. Targeted. Threatened. Shut down. And yet... They stepped up anyway. About that time, Charlie called me. He didn't sound optimistic... He sounded urgent. "Andrew, we've got to move faster." I told him we were. He stopped me. "No. You're not thinking what I'm thinking. I want to be in 35,000 high schools." I actually laughed. "Charlie... there aren't even 35,000 high schools in America." "Okay," he said. "How many are there?" "About 27,000." And without hesitation: "Good. Let's do 27,000." I remember sitting there thinking to myself... we're barely in 1,200 schools. We didn't have the staff. We didn't have the infrastructure. We didn't even have the roadmap yet. But Charlie wasn't fazed. " We'll figure it out." That was him. He didn't wait for perfect conditions. Because he knew something most people don't want to face: If we wait... we lose everything. And now? Less than a year later... We 're in 3,300 schools. Thirteen percent of all high schools in America. Eight states are now backing this effort to put a Club America chapter in every high school statewide. That shouldn 't be possible. Not in this environment. Not with the level of hostility these students face every single day. And yet... it's still happening. But Friend, here 's the part you need to understand: This is not a victory. It's a foothold. Because in the other 87% of schools? There is no resistance. None. Just one-sided propaganda from the Left. One-sided pressure on kids who are too young to even realize what's happening to them. That's the reality. The question isn't whether we're fighting. We are. The question is whether it's enough. Because right now, the students stepping up through Club America... They're not the majority. They 're the exception. They're the ones willing to take the heat. The ones willing to stand alone. The ones willing to risk being targeted just to say: " I love this country." And every time one of those students raises their hand... We have a choice. Back them. Or leave them on their own. Because when a student starts a chapter, we send them an activism kit -- with American flags. Pocket Constitutions. Leadership tools. Everything they need to actually stand their ground. Not symbolically. For real. They've already made the decision to lead. All they're waiting on... is you and me. Each activism kit costs $25. That 's it. $25 to make sure one student doesn't have to stand alone against the Left in a hostile school. $25 to put real tools in their hands. $25 to push back -- even if it's one campus at a time. But here's what gives me hope, Friend... Club America isn't slowing down. It's accelerating. Because every day, more students are stepping forward. Not because it's easy or popular... But because they know what 's at stake. They're starting chapters in schools where they were told not to. They're speaking truth in classrooms where the Left once went unchallenged. They're choosing courage in places designed to make them conform. And they're not alone. They're finding each other. They're bringing more students with them every day. They're building something real -- rooted in faith and freedom, grounded in truth, and unafraid to say that America is worth defending. That's how movements are built. Not from the top down... But from the ground up. One student. One school. One chapter at a time. And Friend -- that's exactly how we take this country back. But only if we move fast enough. Because the Left isn't slowing down. They're not taking a break. They're not afraid to push their anti-American ideas in every classroom they're in. And if we don't match that urgency... if we don't meet that moment with equal conviction... Then the generational window Charlie Kirk opened to save our country closes. And once it closes... It closes for good. That's what's at stake. Let's not waste this moment. Let's back our brave students -- while it still matters. | | For Charlie, Andrew Sypher Chief Field OfficerTurning Point USA P.S. I need you to hear this clearly... Charlie Kirk wasn't just dreaming big when he called me last year about Club America's progress. He was warning us: "The enemy is moving younger. They're coming after students earlier. We don 't have time to wait." And he was right. Look around. Club America may be in 13% of high schools... But in the other 87%? There is no pushback against the Left. No one telling those kids the truth. Just a Leftist pipeline -- from classroom... to belief... to voting booth. And once that pipeline is complete... It 's over. Friend, this is one of the last places a patriot like you can stop it before it 's too late to save our country. You may not be able to step into a hostile high school and stand for truth like these students do. But you can give critical support to a young freedom fighter who will. There's still time to turn this country around... and this is one of the few ways we can actually do it -- one student, one school, one chapter at a time. 4940 East Beverly Road Phoenix, Arizona 85044

Hi Peter, Yesterday, I had the chance to join members of MLK Labor at their rally and picnic in Seattle's South Lake Union neighborhood, celebrating the strength of workers and the power of solidarity. It was a great reminder of why this day matters. I want to recognize the Washington workers who keep our communities running every day. Teachers educating our kids, nurses and health care workers caring for our families, construction workers building our communities, public employees serving their neighbors, agricultural workers feeding our state, service workers keeping businesses moving, and small-business employees helping their communities thrive all deserve our gratitude. If you work hard, you should be able to earn a fair wage, work in a safe environment, and have a meaningful voice in the conditions under which you work. Unions and collective bargaining have long given working people a stronger voice on the job and helped families build greater economic security. That principle remains as important today as ever. As Attorney General, part of protecting Washington workers means enforcing the laws that keep employers from taking advantage of their employees and protecting people when their rights are violated. Every worker should be able to speak up about unlawful treatment and exercise their rights without fear of retaliation. Labor Day is a chance to recognize the dignity of work and the people behind it. I'm grateful for the workers across Washington who show up every day for their families, their coworkers, and their communities. Hey Derek, Here's the deal.
I didn't come to Washington to make consultants happy. I didn't come here to win points with political insiders. And I definitely didn't come here to become another politician who forgets where they came from.
I came here to fight for Pennsylvania. [](https://act.johnfetterman.com/go/53643?t=1&akid=10915%2E434096%2EgmQz0x)
| [DONATE TODAY](https://act.johnfetterman.com/go/53643?t=2&akid=10915%2E434096%2EgmQz0x)
---
Every time I walk onto the Senate floor, I know exactly who I'm thinking about.
* The people working double shifts.
* The guy at the steel mill.
* The nurse pulling another overnight.
* The senior who shouldn't have to choose between medicine and groceries.
* The family wondering why it feels harder every month just to get ahead.

Those are my people.
And they're the reason I'm here.
If you believe Pennsylvania deserves someone who won't forget the people who built Pennsylvania, **[can you chip in a few bucks today?](https://act.johnfetterman.com/go/53643?t=3&akid=10915%2E434096%2EgmQz0x)** | [DONATE TODAY](https://act.johnfetterman.com/go/53643?t=4&akid=10915%2E434096%2EgmQz0x)
---
The truth is, a lot of folks in Washington spend more time talking to each other than they do listening to the people back home.

I'm not interested in that. I'll keep saying what I think. I'll keep voting the way I believe is right.

And I'll keep standing up for the Pennsylvanians who too often get overlooked.

If that sounds like someone worth fighting alongside, I'd really appreciate your support today.
[**Every contribution helps keep this campaign focused on Pennsylvania.**](https://act.johnfetterman.com/go/53643?t=5&akid=10915%2E434096%2EgmQz0x) Thanks for all you do, Derek.
John

WEARE, N.H. — Lily Tang Williams will spend election night at a private gathering at her Weare home with campaign volunteers and staff as results come in. **About Lily Tang Williams**
Born in China just before Mao’s Cultural Revolution to working-class parents, Lily Tang Williams immigrated to the United States with nothing and built a life as an entrepreneur, educator, and community leader in Weare, NH. A living embodiment of the American Dream, she brings a uniquely powerful perspective to the fight for freedom and limited government.

In 2024, Williams won the Republican nomination and captured 47% of the general election vote against current incumbent Maggie Goodlander — coming closer than any Republican has in more than a decade to flipping NH-02. She is back and running stronger than ever in 2026.

**Supporting Planned Parenthood is “sick and twisted??”**
---
Peter,They always say not to read comments on social media, but I just couldn’t resist.

When Michael Alfonso attacked me on Facebook for supporting Planned Parenthood, voters replied and gave him a dose of reality. It backfired on social media and it’s going to backfire on Election Day because health care is important to Northern Wisconsin.

Fellow Patriot,

While millions in dark money floods into Montana to buy this Senate seat, I have been working to earn votes the old fashioned way. I’ve been getting out on the road, meeting with voters, and getting my message out. There’s no replacement for shoe leather.

In the past week alone I was out at PAYS Livestock talking with cattle producers about increasing profitability for this generation of ranchers and the next.

[](http://links.kurtalme.com/u/click?_t=13f02befef694c2ea0e5bfe0ba1ceb44&_m=aee4bbbd97a34bd09fb2a577065d098b&_e=AgXtuRKggm7OEGWb6-BUeWWVspC5P7flmLh8zIemNKl8jaz_rcD-h_veA1SXVma9__0G2-22WCanz9lzu-OYJfIzfzkL_h0GSLmBuSww15qYzGM3auE8c5CGO1Laj0_T-NK3YlRQFu51DmitIyKurOBwj36izvR935aGFuVDCR52OvdMsrVcOszcn2a3iyVOaQM6ZIeeq2Mt_RT6OtMhUpg5_TFV-jZ9qNViVBkbmzeucUAMWid5lwsP18A_WkzFK4dlKN4Cxb7-Yg5wcPykCBf67hHe7snN2nclVlxvsriHtiMRzwoMRwhA1VgorKzxqpBjq0mbk9N9QUFBJAqOJas8C5Itn9lgRgsk7ywQ9ALgV0YXmxiXPyoiqY8pijX22XitOOS0AUIXxwa8-6U8rcU8uV4QqQGd8P08V4dv8LgK8bciNxvkLh5Gt0Y3ohQ7U9wOFB0Zw7m-epFP566q2nu528zGsQFoSPrEHGrhZp62J4Opc24bJdSO1JsY-Y5EtQAe1ctj2Rxrs8SxPqvkG-ZAGDQ2ReihA7Dk3DRqOfRZt-SmNLA46dNnv4mWv7jtY2QSG2H48EmofpnVTOEoam2stedfrVVj1xXlvaEL8HmgboSG1vN79Kx82zY41yBmljfq5ZC8o_QlhYA4PaBlAkSXuqRkLpUaK2_2n_Kw2F3xN_wCHl_kuednUBB6OyxSQMDsKt02DR7PXTWNmVw2fA%3D%3D)

I stopped by Mojo 92.5 to talk about what I am hearing from folks on the trail. I sat down with energy producers to talk about unleashing American energy and creating Montana jobs.
